title.zh: 卷一百一十六 列傳第四十一 二王韋陸二李杜
title.en: Volume 116 Biographies 41: Two Wangs, Wei, Lu, two Li's, Du
title.raw: 卷一百一十六 列傳第四十一 二王韋陸二李杜 Volume 116 Biographies 41: Two Wangs, Wei, Lu, two Li's, Du

sentences.zh: 二王韋陸二李杜

translations.literal: Two Wangs, Wei, Lu, Two Lis, Du.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies: Two Wang Clans, the Wei Clan, Lu Xiangxian, Two Li Clans, and the Du Clan.

sentences.zh: ◎二瑋陸二李杜

translations.literal: ◎ Two Wei, Lu, Two Li, Du.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Two Wei Clans, Lu Xiangxian, Two Li Clans, and the Du Clan.

sentences.zh: 王綝，字方慶，以字顯。

translations.literal: Wang Shen, courtesy name Fangqing, was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen, styled Fangqing, was known by that name.

sentences.zh: 其先自丹楊徙雍咸陽。

translations.literal: His ancestors moved from Danyang to Yong, Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had moved from Danyang to Yong in Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 父弘直，為漢王元昌友。

translations.literal: His father Hongzhi served as Friend to Prince Yuan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Hongzhi was a companion to Prince Yuan of Han.

sentences.zh: 王好畋遊，上書切諫，王稍止，然益疏斥。

translations.literal: The prince loved hunting; he submitted a stern memorial of remonstrance; the prince slightly ceased, yet grew more distant and dismissive.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was fond of the hunt; Hongzhi submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance. The prince eased off somewhat but grew only more distant and cold toward him.

sentences.zh: 終荊王友。

translations.literal: He ended as Friend to the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as companion to the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 方慶起家越王府參軍，受司馬遷、班固二史於記室任希古，希古它遷，就卒其業。

translations.literal: Fangqing began his career as an aide in the Prince of Yue's household; he received Sima Qian's and Ban Gu's two histories from recorder Ren Xigu; when Xigu was transferred elsewhere, he completed the work.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing began as an aide in the household of the Prince of Yue, studying Sima Qian's and Ban Gu's histories under the recorder Ren Xigu. When Xigu was posted elsewhere, Fangqing finished the course of study on his own.

sentences.zh: 武后時，累遷廣州都督。

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu, he was repeatedly promoted to military governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he rose through successive appointments to military governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 南海歲有昆侖舶市外區琛琲，前都督路元睿冒取其貨，舶酋不勝忿，殺之。

translations.literal: In the South Sea each year Kunlun ships came to trade exotic treasures from foreign regions; the previous governor Lu Yuanrui seized their goods by force; the ship chiefs could not bear their rage and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Kunlun merchant vessels called at the South Sea to trade foreign gems and curios. The previous governor Lu Yuanrui had seized their cargo by force; the ship captains, unable to endure the outrage, killed him.

sentences.zh: 方慶至，秋毫無所索。

translations.literal: When Fangqing arrived, he demanded not even a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangqing took office, he exacted not the slightest toll from the traders.

sentences.zh: 始，部中首領沓墨，民詣府訴，府曹素相餉謝，未嘗治。

translations.literal: At first, tribal chiefs in the prefecture were corrupt; the people came to the government office to sue, but the clerks had always exchanged gifts and thanks and never handled the cases.
translations.idiomatic: Before his arrival, local tribal chiefs had been corrupt, and when commoners brought suits to the prefectural yamen the clerks had long taken bribes and returned favors without ever adjudicating a case.

sentences.zh: 方慶約官屬不得與交通，犯者痛論以法，境內清畏。

translations.literal: Fangqing bound his subordinates not to have dealings with outsiders; offenders he punished severely under the law, and within his jurisdiction all grew orderly and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing forbade his staff any private dealings with outsiders and punished violators harshly under the law, until the whole jurisdiction was orderly and awed.

sentences.zh: 議者謂治廣未有如方慶者，號第一，下詔賜瑞錦、雜彩，以著善政。

translations.literal: Commentators said that in governing Guang there had been none like Fangqing; he was ranked first; an edict bestowed auspicious brocade and assorted silks to mark his good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said that Guang had never been governed as well as under Fangqing, who was ranked first among governors. The court issued an edict granting him auspicious brocade and colored silks in recognition of his excellent administration.

sentences.zh: 轉洛州長史，封石泉縣子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief administrator of Luozhou and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiquan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief administrator of Luozhou and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 遷鸞臺侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，進鳳閣侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Luan Terrace, made co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace, and advanced to vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of the Luan Terrace, appointed associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace, and then advanced to vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 神功初，清邊道大總管武攸宜破契丹凱還，且獻俘，內史王及善以孝明帝忌月，請鼓吹備而不作，方慶曰：「晉穆帝納後，當康帝忌月，時以為疑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenggong era, the grand commander of the Qingbian circuit Wu Youyi defeated the Khitan in triumph and returned, about to present captives; the palace secretary Wang Jishan, citing the mourning month for Emperor Xiaoming of Han, asked that the martial music be prepared but not played. Fangqing said: 'When Emperor Mu of Jin took a consort, it fell in the mourning month for Emperor Kang; at the time this was held doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenggong era, Wu Youyi, grand commander of the Qingbian circuit, defeated the Khitan and returned in triumph to present captives. The palace secretary Wang Jishan, citing the mourning month for Emperor Xiaoming of Han, asked that the martial drums and pipes be set out but not sounded. Fangqing said: 'When Emperor Mu of Jin took a consort, the month coincided with the mourning observance for Emperor Kang, and contemporaries were uncertain what to do.

sentences.zh: 荀詢謂《禮》有忌日無忌月，自月而推，則忌時忌年，愈無理據。

translations.literal: Xun Xun said that the Rites provide mourning days but not mourning months; if one extends from months, then mourning hours and mourning years would follow, which grows ever more without rational basis.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xun argued that the Rites prescribe mourning days, not mourning months; extend the logic to months and one would have mourning hours and mourning years as well—an ever less tenable position.

sentences.zh: 世用其言。

translations.literal: The age adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed his view.

sentences.zh: 臣謂軍方大凱，作樂無嫌。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the army has just won a great triumph; to perform music is without offense.'
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the army has just won a great victory and that music on this occasion is unobjectionable.'

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved his view.

sentences.zh: 武后幸玉泉祠，以山道險，欲禦腰輿。

translations.literal: Empress Wu visited the Jade Spring Shrine; because the mountain road was perilous, she wished to ride in a waist litter.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu visited the Jade Spring Shrine, she found the mountain road treacherous and wished to ride in a waist litter.

sentences.zh: 方慶奏：「昔張猛諫漢元帝『乘船危，就橋安』。

translations.literal: Fangqing memorialized: 'In former times Zhang Meng remonstrated with Emperor Yuan of Han, "Taking a boat is perilous; taking the bridge is safe.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing memorialized: 'Long ago Zhang Meng warned Emperor Yuan of Han that taking a boat was perilous while taking the bridge was safe.

sentences.zh: 帝乃從橋。

translations.literal: The emperor then took the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then used the bridge.

sentences.zh: 今山阿危峭，隥道曲狹，比於樓船，又復甚危，陛下奈何輕踐畏塗哉？」

translations.literal: Now the mountain slopes are steep and precipitous, the hidden paths winding and narrow—compared with a tower ship they are yet more dangerous. How can Your Majesty lightly tread such a path of dread?'
translations.idiomatic: Today these mountain slopes are sheer and the hidden paths narrow and twisting—more dangerous still than any tower ship. How can Your Majesty lightly set foot on such a fearful route?'

sentences.zh: 後為罷行。

translations.literal: The empress thereafter abandoned the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then abandoned the trip.

sentences.zh: 方慶嘗以「令，期及大功喪，未葬，不聽朝賀；

translations.literal: Fangqing once cited the statute: 'When the mourning period reaches that for a parent or when the greater mourning obligation applies, before burial one may not attend court congratulations;
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing once cited the statute: 'During the mourning period for a parent, or during the greater mourning obligation before burial, one may not attend court congratulations;

sentences.zh: 未除，弗豫享宴。

translations.literal: before the mourning is ended, one may not take part in banquets.
translations.idiomatic: before the mourning is ended, one may not join in feasts and banquets.

sentences.zh: 比群臣不遵用，頹紊教誼，不可長」。

translations.literal: Yet now the ministers do not observe this; they have let ritual teaching fall into disorder—this cannot be allowed to continue.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet ministers now ignore these rules and let ritual discipline decay—this cannot be allowed to go on.'

sentences.zh: 有詔申責，內外畏之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to rebuke them sternly, and within and without the court all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued rebuking the offenders, and throughout the court and bureaucracy all stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 後嘗就求義之書，方慶奏：「十世從祖義之書四十餘番，太宗求之，先臣番上送，今所存惟一軸。

translations.literal: Later she once asked him for the calligraphy of Yizhi; Fangqing memorialized: 'My tenth-generation collateral ancestor Yizhi left more than forty scrolls of writing; Emperor Taizong requested them and my forebear presented them in turn; what remains today is only one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: The empress once asked him for the calligraphy of Wang Yizhi. Fangqing memorialized: 'My tenth-generation collateral ancestor Yizhi left more than forty scrolls of writing. Emperor Taizong requested them, and my forebear presented them in succession; only one scroll survives today.

sentences.zh: 並上十一世祖導、十世祖洽、九世祖珣、八世祖曇首、七世祖僧綽、六世祖仲寶、五世祖騫、高祖規、曾祖褒並九世從祖獻之等凡二十八人書共十篇。」

translations.literal: I also present the writings of my eleventh-generation ancestor Dao, tenth-generation ancestor Qia, ninth-generation ancestor Xun, eighth-generation ancestor Tanshou, seventh-generation ancestor Sengchuo, sixth-generation ancestor Zhongbao, fifth-generation ancestor Qian, great-grandfather Gui, great-great-grandfather Bao, and ninth-generation collateral ancestor Xianzhi—twenty-eight men in all, ten pieces of writing.'
translations.idiomatic: I also present the writings of my eleventh-generation ancestor Wang Dao, tenth-generation Wang Qia, ninth-generation Wang Xun, eighth-generation Wang Tanshou, seventh-generation Wang Sengchuo, sixth-generation Wang Zhongbao, fifth-generation Wang Qian, great-grandfather Wang Gui, great-great-grandfather Wang Bao, and ninth-generation collateral ancestor Wang Xianzhi—twenty-eight men in all, comprising ten scrolls.'

sentences.zh: 後禦武成殿遍示群臣，詔中書舍人崔融序其代閥，號《寶章集》，復以賜方慶，士人歆其寵。

translations.literal: Later at the Wucheng Hall she displayed them to all the ministers and ordered the Secretariat drafter Cui Rong to compose a preface on their lineage, titling the collection Precious Scrolls; she then bestowed it again on Fangqing, and gentlemen marveled at his favor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress later displayed the collection throughout the Wucheng Hall for all ministers to see, ordered the Secretariat drafter Cui Rong to write a preface tracing their lineage, and titled the anthology Precious Scrolls. She then bestowed the collection on Fangqing again, to the envy of the scholarly class.

sentences.zh: 以老乞身，改麟臺監，脩國史。

translations.literal: Citing age, he begged to retire and was made director of the Lin Terrace, editing the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Citing old age, he requested retirement and was appointed director of the Lin Terrace to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 中宗復為皇太子，拜方慶檢校左庶子。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was again made crown prince, Fangqing was appointed acting left guardian of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored as crown prince, Fangqing was appointed acting left guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 後欲季冬講武，有司不時辦，遂用明年孟春。

translations.literal: Later the emperor wished to hold martial exercises in the last month of winter; the offices could not prepare in time, so they used the first month of spring of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later wished to hold martial exercises in the last month of winter, but the responsible offices could not prepare in time, so the drill was scheduled for the first month of spring the following year.

sentences.zh: 方慶曰：「按《月令》『孟冬，天子命將帥講武，習射禦，角力。』

translations.literal: Fangqing said: 'According to the Monthly Ordinances, "In the first month of winter the Son of Heaven orders the generals to conduct martial exercises, practice archery and defense, and test strength.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing said: 'According to the Monthly Ordinances, "In the first month of winter the Son of Heaven orders his commanders to conduct martial exercises, practice archery and defense, and test strength.

sentences.zh: 此乃三時務農，一時講武，安不忘危之道。

translations.literal: This is the way of three seasons devoted to agriculture and one season to martial training—security without forgetting peril.
translations.idiomatic: This is the principle of three seasons for farming and one for martial training—peace without forgetting danger.

sentences.zh: 孟春不可以稱兵。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring one may not raise arms.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring one may not take up arms.

sentences.zh: 兵，金也，金勝木。

translations.literal: Arms belong to metal; metal overcomes wood.
translations.idiomatic: Arms belong to the element metal, and metal overcomes wood.

sentences.zh: 方春木王，而舉金以害盛德，逆生氣。

translations.literal: Just as spring is the reign of wood, to raise metal and harm the flourishing virtue is to go against the breath of life.
translations.idiomatic: Spring is the season when wood holds sway; to raise metal and injure that flourishing virtue is to oppose the vital force of growth.

sentences.zh: 孟春行冬令，則水潦為敗，雪霜大摯，首種不入。

translations.literal: If in the first month of spring one executes winter ordinances, floods become ruinous, frost and snow severe, and the first sowing fails to take root.
translations.idiomatic: If winter ordinances are enforced in the first month of spring, floods will ruin the land, frost and snow will be severe, and the first sowing will fail.

sentences.zh: 今孟春講武，以陰政犯陽氣，害發生之德，臣恐水潦敗物，霜雪損稼，夏麥不登。

translations.literal: Now to conduct martial exercises in the first month of spring is to let yin governance violate yang qi and harm the virtue of generation; your subject fears floods will ruin things, frost and snow will harm the crops, and the summer wheat will not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: To hold martial exercises in the first month of spring is to let yin governance violate yang energy and harm the virtue of growth. I fear floods will destroy the harvest, frost and snow will damage the grain, and the summer wheat will fail.

sentences.zh: 願陛下不違時令，前及孟冬，以順天道。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty not violate the seasons but advance the date to the first month of winter, to accord with Heaven's way.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty not to violate the seasons but to schedule the exercises no later than the first month of winter, in accord with Heaven's way.'

sentences.zh: 手制褒允。

translations.literal: An imperial note in his own hand praised and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a note in his own hand praising and approving the memorial.

sentences.zh: 是歲，真拜左庶子，進封公，奉入同職事三品，兼侍太子讀書，方慶奏人臣於天子，未有斥子名者。

translations.literal: That year he was formally appointed left guardian of the heir, advanced to duke, given salary equal to third rank, and also charged to attend the crown prince in study. Fangqing memorialized that a subject addressing the Son of Heaven had never spoken the heir's personal name aloud.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was formally appointed left guardian of the heir, advanced to duke, granted salary equal to third rank, and charged to attend the crown prince in his studies. Fangqing memorialized that no subject addressing the Son of Heaven had ever spoken the heir's personal name aloud.

sentences.zh: 晉山濤啟事，稱皇太子不名，孝敬為太子，，更『弘』為『崇』；

translations.literal: In Jin, Shan Tao's memorials referred to the crown prince without naming him; when Xiaojing was crown prince, 'Hong' was changed to 'Chong';
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Shan Tao's memorials referred to the crown prince without naming him; when the heir Xiaojing held the title, the character Hong was changed to Chong;

sentences.zh: 沛王為太子，更『賢』為『文』。

translations.literal: when the Prince of Pei was crown prince, 'Xian' was changed to 'Wen.'
translations.idiomatic: when the Prince of Pei was crown prince, the character Xian was changed to Wen.

sentences.zh: 今東宮門殿名多嫌觸，請一改之，以協舊典。」

translations.literal: Now many names in the Eastern Palace halls taboo the heir's name; I beg that they be changed to accord with former precedent.'
translations.idiomatic: Many names in the Eastern Palace halls now taboo the heir's name; I beg that they be changed to accord with established precedent.'

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 長安二年卒，贈兗州都督，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Chang'an and was posthumously made military governor of Yanzhou, with the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Chang'an era and was posthumously appointed military governor of Yanzhou, with the posthumous name Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 中宗復位，以東宮舊臣，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was restored to the throne, as a former Eastern Palace minister he was posthumously made minister of the civil service.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored to the throne, Fangqing was posthumously appointed minister of the civil service as a former Eastern Palace counselor.

sentences.zh: 方慶博學，練朝章，著書二百餘篇，尤精《三禮》。

translations.literal: Fangqing was broadly learned, skilled in court regulations, and wrote more than two hundred treatises, especially expert in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing was broadly learned and thoroughly versed in court regulations. He wrote more than two hundred treatises and was especially expert in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 學者有所咨質，酬復淵詣，故門人次為《雜禮答問》。

translations.literal: When scholars consulted him, his replies were profound and to the point; therefore his disciples compiled Miscellaneous Answers on Ritual Questions.
translations.idiomatic: When scholars consulted him, his replies were profound and exact, and his disciples later compiled them as Miscellaneous Answers on Ritual Questions.

sentences.zh: 家聚書多，不減秘府，圖畫皆異本。

translations.literal: His household gathered many books, not fewer than the imperial archive; paintings and calligraphy were all rare editions.
translations.idiomatic: His household held a library rivaling the imperial archive, and its paintings and calligraphy were all rare editions.

sentences.zh: 方慶歿後，諸子不能業，隨皆散亡。

translations.literal: After Fangqing's death his sons could not maintain the collection, and it all scattered and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: After Fangqing's death his sons could not maintain the collection, and it was scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 孫俌。

translations.literal: His grandson Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 六世孫玙，別傳。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation descendant Yu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation descendant Wang Yu is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 玙曾孫摶。

translations.literal: Yu's great-grandson Tuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's great-grandson Wang Tuan.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：李德裕著書稱：「方慶為相時，子為眉州司士參軍。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Li Deyu wrote in a book: 'When Fangqing was chief minister, his son was a judicial aide in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Li Deyu wrote in one of his works: 'When Fangqing served as chief minister, his son held the post of judicial aide in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 武后曰：『君在相位，何子之遠？』

translations.literal: Empress Wu said: "You hold the highest office—why is your son so far away?'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said, "You hold the highest office—why is your son posted so far away?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：『盧陵是陛下愛子，今尚在遠，臣之子庸敢相近？』

translations.literal: He replied: 'Luling is Your Majesty's beloved son and is still far away—how would your subject's son dare to be posted nearby?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Luling is Your Majesty's beloved son and is still posted far away—how would this subject's son dare to seek a nearby appointment?

sentences.zh: 以比倉唐悟文侯事。」

translations.literal: He compared this to Cang Tang's enlightening Duke Wen of Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: Li compared this to the story of Cang Tang enlightening Duke Wen of Wei.'

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，君子哉！

translations.literal: Alas—a gentleman indeed!
translations.idiomatic: What a gentleman he was!

sentences.zh: 雖造次不忘悟君於善。

translations.literal: Even in haste he did not forget to awaken his lord to what is good.
translations.idiomatic: Even in haste he never forgot to guide his sovereign toward what is right.

sentences.zh: 及建言不斥太子名，以動群臣，示中興之漸，所謂人難言者，於方慶難乎哉！

translations.literal: And when he proposed not speaking the crown prince's name aloud, to move the ministers and show the first signs of restoration—what men find hard to say, was it hard for Fangqing!
translations.idiomatic: When he proposed that the crown prince's name not be spoken aloud, moving the ministers and signaling the first stirrings of restoration—what others find hard to say, was it hard for Fangqing!

sentences.zh: 德裕之稱，為不誣矣。

translations.literal: Deyu's praise was not false.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu's praise was not misplaced.

sentences.zh: 俌字靈龜。

translations.literal: Fu's courtesy name was Linggui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, styled Linggui.

sentences.zh: 明經，調莫州參軍，辟范陽節度使張守珪幕府。

translations.literal: He passed the classics examination, was appointed aide in Mozhou, and was recruited into the staff of Zhang Shougui, military governor of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the classics examination, was appointed aide in Mozhou, and was recruited into the staff of Zhang Shougui, military governor of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 時契丹屈烈部將謀入寇，河北騷然。

translations.literal: At the time the Qulie division of the Khitan was about to plot an invasion, and Hebei was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Qulie division of the Khitan was plotting an invasion, and Hebei was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 俌至虜中，脅說禍福，虜乃不入。

translations.literal: Fu went among the barbarians, pressed upon them the consequences of fortune and disaster, and the barbarians then did not invade.
translations.idiomatic: Fu went among the Khitan, pressed upon them the consequences of war and peace, and they abandoned the invasion.

sentences.zh: 安祿山叛，拜博陵、常山二太守，副河北招討。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he was appointed prefect of both Boling and Changshan and deputy to the Hebei campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he was appointed prefect of Boling and Changshan and deputy commander of the Hebei suppression force.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made minister of imperial sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed minister of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 自褒至俌，六世封石泉雲。

translations.literal: From Bao to Fu, six generations held the enfeoffment of Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Bao to Wang Fu, six generations held the enfeoffment of Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 俌孫遂。

translations.literal: Fu's grandson Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's grandson Wang Sui.

sentences.zh: 遂好興利，操下以嚴。

translations.literal: Sui loved to promote profit and governed subordinates with severity.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was eager to promote revenue and ruled his subordinates with harsh discipline.

sentences.zh: 累遷鄧州刺史、太府卿、西北供軍使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Dengzhou, minister of the granaries, and commissioner for supplying the northwest armies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to prefect of Dengzhou, minister of the granaries, and commissioner for supplying the northwest armies.

sentences.zh: 與度支潘孟陽爭營田事，憲宗怒，出遂為柳州刺史。

translations.literal: He quarreled with the revenue commissioner Pan Mengyang over military colony lands; Emperor Xianzong was angry and sent Sui out as prefect of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with the revenue commissioner Pan Mengyang over military colony lands. Emperor Xianzong was angered and sent Sui out as prefect of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 親吏韋行素、柳季常當受課料兩池，吏見遂斥，即抵以罪。

translations.literal: His trusted clerks Wei Xingsu and Liu Jichang were to receive the tax proceeds of two ponds; when the clerks saw Sui dismissed, they immediately charged him with crimes.
translations.idiomatic: His trusted clerks Wei Xingsu and Liu Jichang were entitled to the tax proceeds of two ponds. When they saw Sui demoted, they immediately brought charges against him.

sentences.zh: 始，詔書出，左丞呂元膺劾：「遂補吏犯贓，法當坐，而詔稱『清能業官』，按遂犯有狀，不宜謂清。

translations.literal: At first, when the edict was issued, the left vice director Lü Yuanying impeached him: 'Sui's clerks committed bribery and by law should be punished, yet the edict calls him "upright and able in office." Investigating Sui's offenses, there is evidence against him; he should not be called upright.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment edict was first issued, the left vice director Lü Yuanying impeached him: 'Sui's clerks committed bribery and should be punished by law, yet the edict calls him "upright and able in office." Investigation shows offenses with evidence against Sui; he should not be called upright.

sentences.zh: 且柳，大州，不可使治。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Liu is a great prefecture and should not be given him to govern.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Liuzhou is a major prefecture and should not be entrusted to him.'

sentences.zh: 帝喻之，乃下。

translations.literal: The emperor explained the matter to him, and the appointment then went through.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor explained the matter to Lü, and the appointment then went through.

sentences.zh: 會兵宿淮西，亟財賦，藉遂幹強，拜宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: As troops were encamped in Huaixi and revenue was urgently needed, they relied on Sui's forceful ability and appointed him military governor of Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: As troops were encamped in Huaixi and revenue was urgently needed, the court relied on Sui's forceful ability and appointed him military governor of Xuan and She.

sentences.zh: 蔡已平，師東討李師道，召為光祿卿、淄青行營糧料使。

translations.literal: After Cai was pacified, the army marched east to attack Li Shidao; he was summoned as minister of imperial entertainments and commissary for the Ziqing campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai Prefecture was pacified, the army marched east against Li Shidao. Sui was summoned as minister of imperial entertainments and commissary for the Ziqing campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 辭卿職，換檢校左散騎常侍，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: He declined the ministerial post and was instead made acting left regular attendant and concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the ministerial post and was instead made acting left regular attendant with the concurrent title of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 始，調兵食歲三百萬，俄而賊誅，遂簿羨貲百萬以獻，帝高其能。

translations.literal: At first three million in provisions for the troops was requisitioned yearly; soon the rebel was executed, and Sui recorded a surplus of one million and presented it; the emperor admired his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Three million in provisions for the troops had initially been requisitioned each year. Soon the rebel was killed, and Sui recorded a surplus of one million and presented it to the throne. The emperor admired his efficiency.

sentences.zh: 於時析齊為三鎮，即拜遂沂兗海觀察使。

translations.literal: At that time Qi was divided into three circuits, and Sui was immediately appointed military governor of Yi, Yan, and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was then divided into three circuits, and Sui was immediately appointed military governor of Yi, Yan, and Hai.

sentences.zh: 遂資褊刻，仗撲皆逾制。

translations.literal: Sui was by nature narrow and harsh; his beating staffs all exceeded regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was narrow-minded and harsh by nature, and his beating staffs all exceeded the prescribed size.

sentences.zh: 盛夏，治署舍墻垣，程督慘峭。

translations.literal: In the height of summer he had the government offices and walls repaired, driving the work with cruel severity.
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer he had the government offices and perimeter walls repaired, driving the labor with brutal severity.

sentences.zh: 將吏素悍戾，遂輒罵曰：「反殘賊！」

translations.literal: The officers and clerks were by nature fierce and defiant; Sui would curse them, saying: 'Rebel brutes!'
translations.idiomatic: His officers and clerks were by nature fierce and defiant. Sui would curse them: 'Rebel brutes!'

sentences.zh: 人人羞忿。

translations.literal: Every man burned with shame and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Every man burned with shame and rage.

sentences.zh: 裨校王弁與役人浴於川，語曰：「天方雨，墻且毀，等罪耳！」

translations.literal: The adjutant Wang Bian bathed in the river with the laborers and said: 'Heaven is about to rain; the walls will collapse anyway—it's the same crime either way!'
translations.idiomatic: The adjutant Wang Bian bathed in the river with the laborers and said, 'Rain is coming—the walls will collapse anyway. The penalty is the same either way!'

sentences.zh: 乃謀亂。

translations.literal: They then plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: They then plotted a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂方燕，弁率其黨挾兵進，遂驚，匿廁下，執而數其罪，殺之。

translations.literal: The next day, while Sui was at a banquet, Bian led his faction in with weapons; Sui was startled, hid beneath the privy, was seized and his crimes enumerated, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, while Sui was at a banquet, Bian led his faction in armed. Sui fled in alarm and hid beneath the privy. They seized him, recited his crimes, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其副張敦實、官屬李矩甫皆死。

translations.literal: His deputy Zhang Dunshi and the official Li Jufu also died.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Zhang Dunshi and the official Li Jufu were also killed.

sentences.zh: 弁自知留事。

translations.literal: Bian himself took charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bian himself assumed control of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝以沂、海新定，畏青、鄆亦搖，乃拜弁開州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yi and Hai had only just been pacified and feared Qing and Yun might also be shaken, appointed Bian prefect of Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yi and Hai had only just been pacified and the court feared Qing and Yun might also be shaken, the emperor appointed Bian prefect of Kai as a placatory measure.

sentences.zh: 至徐州，械送京師，斬東市。

translations.literal: When he reached Xuzhou he was placed in the cangue and sent to the capital, and was executed at the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xuzhou he was placed in fetters and sent to the capital, where he was executed at the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 監軍上遂所制杖，出示於朝為戒雲。

translations.literal: The army supervisor presented the staffs Sui had had made and displayed them at court as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor presented the oversized staffs Sui had had made and displayed them at court as a warning to other governors.

sentences.zh: 摶字昭逸。

translations.literal: Tuan's courtesy name was Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan, styled Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，辟佐王鐸滑州節度府，累遷蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was recruited as aide in Wang Duo’s Huazhou military governorship, and was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, joined the staff of Wang Duo as military governor of Huazhou, and rose through successive appointments to prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，以戶部侍郎判戶部。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made vice minister of revenue with charge of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed vice minister of revenue with executive charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianning era he was advanced to co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianning era he was promoted to co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 董昌誅，出為威勝節度使。

translations.literal: After Dong Chang was executed he was sent out as military governor of Weisheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong Chang was executed he was sent out as military governor of Weisheng.

sentences.zh: 未行，加檢校尚書右僕射、浙東西宣撫使。

translations.literal: Before he departed he was additionally made acting right vice director of the secretariat and commissioner to pacify eastern and western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was additionally appointed acting right vice director of the secretariat and commissioner to pacify eastern and western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 會錢寔兼領二浙，故留拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事、判度支。

translations.literal: As Qian Liu concurrently held both Zhe circuits, he was therefore kept at court and appointed vice director of the Chancellery, co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and with charge of the revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qian Liu was already holding both Zhe circuits, Tuan was kept at court and appointed vice director of the Chancellery, co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and with charge of the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 昭宗建嫡後，摶請因赦天下以尊大其禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong established the legitimate heir, Tuan requested that a general amnesty be used to magnify the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong established the legitimate heir, Tuan requested that a general amnesty be proclaimed to magnify the ceremonial observance.

sentences.zh: 正拜右僕射，遷司空，封魯國公。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed right vice director, transferred to minister of works, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed right vice director, promoted to minister of works, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 初，中官權盛，帝欲翦抑之。

translations.literal: At first the eunuchs’ power was great and the emperor wished to cut them down.
translations.idiomatic: At first the eunuchs held great power, and the emperor wished to curb them.

sentences.zh: 自石門還，政一決宰相，群宦不平，構藩鎮內脅天子。

translations.literal: After returning from Shimen, policy was decided solely by the chief ministers; the eunuchs were discontent and incited the military governors to coerce the emperor from within.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Shimen, policy was decided solely by the chief ministers. The eunuchs were discontent and incited the military governors to pressure the emperor from within.

sentences.zh: 摶曰：「人君務平心大體，禦萬物，偏聽產亂，古所戒也。

translations.literal: Tuan said: 'A ruler should keep an even heart and grasp the great pattern, governing all things; partial listening breeds disorder—this the ancients warned against.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan said, 'A ruler should keep an even heart and grasp the great pattern, governing all things under heaven. Partial listening breeds disorder—this the ancients warned against.

sentences.zh: 今奄人盜威福，逼制君上，道路人皆知之。

translations.literal: Now the eunuchs steal authority and blessings and coerce the sovereign; everyone on the roads knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Now the eunuchs usurp authority and coerce the sovereign—everyone on the roads knows it.

sentences.zh: 方朝廷多難，未可卒除，當徐以計去之。

translations.literal: The court is now in many difficulties and they cannot be removed at once; they should be removed gradually by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The court faces many difficulties and they cannot be removed at once; they should be removed gradually by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 事急，且有變。」

translations.literal: If matters are rushed, there will be upheaval.'
translations.idiomatic: If matters are rushed, upheaval will follow.'

sentences.zh: 崔胤與摶並位，素忌摶明達有謀，即劾摶為中官外應。

translations.literal: Cui Yin shared office with Tuan and had long resented Tuan’s clarity and resourcefulness; he immediately impeached Tuan as the eunuchs’ outside ally.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin shared office with Tuan and had long resented his clarity and resourcefulness. He immediately impeached Tuan as the eunuchs’ outside ally.

sentences.zh: 會胤罷宰相，疑摶擠斥，乃厚結朱全忠薦己復輔政，即誣摶與樞密使宋道弼、景務脩交私，將危社稷。

translations.literal: When Yin was dismissed as chief minister he suspected Tuan had driven him out; he therefore cultivated Zhu Quanzhong thickly to recommend his own return to government, and slandered Tuan as having private dealings with the privy commissioners Song Daobi and Jing Wuxiu that would endanger the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was dismissed as chief minister he suspected Tuan had engineered his removal. He cultivated Zhu Quanzhong heavily to recommend his own return to power and slandered Tuan as having private dealings with the privy commissioners Song Daobi and Jing Wuxiu that would endanger the state.

sentences.zh: 全忠因顯疏其尤。

translations.literal: Quanzhong thereupon submitted an open memorial detailing the worst charges.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong thereupon submitted an open memorial detailing the gravest charges.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，罷為工部侍即，貶溪州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua he was dismissed to vice minister of public works and demoted to prefect of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Guanghua era he was dismissed to vice minister of public works and demoted to prefect of Xi.

sentences.zh: 又貶崖州司戶參軍事，賜死藍田驛。

translations.literal: He was further demoted to registrar of Yazhou and ordered to take his own life at the Lantian post station.
translations.idiomatic: He was further demoted to registrar of Yazhou and ordered to take his own life at the Lantian post station.

sentences.zh: 韋思謙，名仁約，以近武后父諱為嫌，遂以字行。

translations.literal: Wei Sizhi, personal name Renyue, because it was close to Empress Wu’s father’s taboo name, therefore went by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sizhi, personal name Renyue, was too close to the taboo name of Empress Wu’s father and therefore went by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 其先出雍州杜陵，後客襄陽，更徙為鄭州陽武人。

translations.literal: His ancestors came from Duling in Yongzhou; later they sojourned in Xiangyang and finally moved to become natives of Yangwu in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors came from Duling in Yongzhou; later the family sojourned in Xiangyang and finally settled as natives of Yangwu in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八歲喪母，以孝聞。

translations.literal: At eight he lost his mother and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at eight and was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，累調應城令，負殿，不得進官。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination he was repeatedly assigned as magistrate of Yingcheng; he owed arrears in taxes and could not advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was repeatedly assigned as magistrate of Yingcheng. He owed tax arrears and could not advance in office.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書高季輔曰：「予始得此一人，豈以小疵棄大德邪？」

translations.literal: The minister of the civil service Gao Jifu said: 'I have just found this one man—how could I discard great virtue for a small flaw?'
translations.idiomatic: The minister of the civil service Gao Jifu said, 'I have just found this one man—how could I discard great virtue for a small flaw?'

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「御史出使，不能動搖山嶽，震懾州縣，為不任職。」

translations.literal: He often said: 'When a censor goes on mission, if he cannot shake mountains and rivers and awe prefectures and counties, he is not fit for office.'
translations.idiomatic: He often said, 'When a censor goes on mission, if he cannot shake mountains and rivers and awe prefectures and counties, he is not fit for office.'

sentences.zh: 中書令褚遂良市地不如直，思謙劾之，罷為同州刺史。

translations.literal: The chief minister Chu Suiliang purchased land below fair value; Sizhi impeached him and he was dismissed to prefect of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Chu Suiliang purchased land below fair value. Sizhi impeached him, and Suiliang was dismissed to prefect of Tong.

sentences.zh: 及復相，出思謙清水令。

translations.literal: When he returned as chief minister, Sizhi was sent out as magistrate of Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: When Suiliang returned as chief minister, Sizhi was sent out as magistrate of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 或吊之，答曰：「吾狷直，觸機輒發，暇恤身乎？

translations.literal: When someone condoled with him he replied: 'I am blunt and upright; when I touch a trigger I fire—when would I spare myself?
translations.idiomatic: When someone condoled with him he replied, 'I am blunt and upright; when I touch a trigger I fire—when would I spare myself?

sentences.zh: 丈夫當敢言地，要須明目張膽以報天子，焉能錄錄保妻子邪？」

translations.literal: A man should speak boldly where it matters; he must open his eyes wide and report to the Son of Heaven—how can he cringe and protect wife and children?'
translations.idiomatic: A man should speak boldly where it matters; he must open his eyes wide and report to the Son of Heaven—how can he cringe and protect only wife and children?'

sentences.zh: 沛王府長史皇甫公義引為倉曹參軍，謂曰：「公非池中物，屈公為數旬客，以重吾府。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Pei’s chief administrator Huangfu Gongyi recruited him as granary aide and told him: 'You are no creature of a pond; I bend you to be my guest for a few weeks to lend weight to my household.'
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pei's chief administrator Huangfu Gongyi recruited him as granary aide and told him, 'You are no creature of a pond; I bend you to be my guest for a few weeks to lend weight to my household.'

sentences.zh: 改侍御史，高宗賢之，每召與語，雖甚倦，徙倚軒檻，猶數刻罷。

translations.literal: He was changed to attendant censor; Emperor Gaozong esteemed him and summoned him to talk; even when very weary, leaning on the balustrade, he would still talk for several quarters of an hour before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant censor. Emperor Gaozong esteemed him and summoned him for conversation; even when very weary, leaning on the balustrade, the emperor would still talk with him for a quarter of an hour or more before stopping.

sentences.zh: 疑獄劇事，多與參裁。

translations.literal: Doubtful cases and urgent matters were largely referred to him for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Doubtful cases and urgent matters were largely referred to him for judgment.

sentences.zh: 武候將軍田仁會誣奏御史張仁祎，帝廷詰，仁祎懦不得對。

translations.literal: The Wuhou general Tian Renhui falsely memorialized against the censor Zhang Renyi; the emperor questioned him at court, and Renyi in cowardice could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhou general Tian Renhui falsely memorialized against the censor Zhang Renyi. The emperor questioned Renyi at court, but in cowardice he could not answer.

sentences.zh: 思謙為辯其枉，因言仁會營罔陷人不測者，詞旨詳暢，帝善之，仁祎得不坐。

translations.literal: Sizhi argued his innocence and went on to say that Renhui schemed to entrap people unpredictably; his words were detailed and fluent; the emperor approved, and Renyi was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi argued his innocence and went on to say that Renhui schemed unpredictably to entrap people. His words were detailed and fluent; the emperor approved, and Renyi was not punished.

sentences.zh: 累遷右司郎中、尚書左丞，振明綱轄，朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to right bureau director and left vice director of the secretariat, clarifying regulations, and the court grew orderly and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to right bureau director and left vice director of the secretariat, clarifying regulations until the court grew orderly and solemn.

sentences.zh: 進御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was advanced to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 性謇諤，顏色莊重，不可犯。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and outspoken, his bearing solemn and not to be transgressed.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was blunt and outspoken, with a solemn bearing that brooked no offense.

sentences.zh: 見王公，未嘗屈禮。

translations.literal: When he met princes and dukes he never bent ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When he met princes and dukes he never bent ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 或以為譏，答曰：「耳目官固當特立。

translations.literal: Some took this as criticism; he replied: 'Officers of the senses and ears should by rights stand apart.
translations.idiomatic: Some took this as criticism. He replied, 'Officers of the senses and ears should by rights stand apart.

sentences.zh: 雕、鶚、鷹、鹯，豈眾禽之偶，奈何屈以狎之？」

translations.literal: The eagle, the osprey, the hawk, and the falcon—how could they be mates of common birds? Why bend to be familiar with them?'
translations.idiomatic: The eagle, the osprey, the hawk, and the falcon—how could they be mates of common birds? Why bend to be familiar with them?'

sentences.zh: 帝崩，思謙扶疾入臨，涕泗冰須，俯伏號絕，詔給扶侍。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Sizhi, supporting himself though ill, came to mourn; tears and mucus froze his beard; he prostrated himself and cried until he fainted; an edict granted him attendants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Sizhi came to mourn though ill, his tears freezing on his beard. He prostrated himself and cried until he fainted. An edict granted him attendants to support him.

sentences.zh: 轉司屬卿，復為右肅政大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Bureau of Dependents and again made right rectifier-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Bureau of Dependents and again made right rectifier-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 故事，大夫與御史鈞禮，思謙獨不答。

translations.literal: By precedent the chief and the censors exchanged equal courtesy; Sizhi alone did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the chief and the censors exchanged equal courtesy; Sizhi alone did not respond.

sentences.zh: 或以為疑，思謙曰：「班列固有差，奈何尚姑息邪？」

translations.literal: Some found this doubtful; Sizhi said: 'Rank in the procession naturally has distinctions—why still indulge?'
translations.idiomatic: Some found this doubtful. Sizhi said, 'Rank in the procession naturally has distinctions—why still indulge?'

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，封博昌縣男，同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chuigong era he was enfeoffed as Baron of Bochang and made third rank with the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chuigong era he was enfeoffed as Baron of Bochang and made third rank with the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 轉納言，辭疾，不許，詔肩輿以朝，聽子孫侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace secretary; he pleaded illness but was not permitted; an edict ordered him carried in a sedan chair to court and allowed his sons and grandsons to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace secretary. He pleaded illness but was not permitted to retire. An edict ordered him carried in a sedan chair to court and allowed his sons and grandsons to attend him.

sentences.zh: 以太中大夫致仕，卒，贈幽州都督。

translations.literal: He retired as grand master of palace attendance and died; he was posthumously made military governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as grand master of palace attendance and died. He was posthumously appointed military governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子承慶、嗣立。

translations.literal: His sons were Chengqing and Silin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wei Chengqing and Wei Silin.

sentences.zh: 承慶字延休。

translations.literal: Chengqing's courtesy name was Yanxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing, styled Yanxiu.

sentences.zh: 性謹畏，事繼母為篤孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was cautious and fearful, and in serving his stepmother he was deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was cautious and reverent, and in serving his stepmother he was deeply filial.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，補雍王府參軍，府中文翰悉委之。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed aide in the Prince of Yong's household, and all the household's literary documents were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed aide in the Prince of Yong's household, to whom all literary documents were entrusted.

sentences.zh: 王為太子，遷司議郎。

translations.literal: When the prince became crown prince, he was transferred to remonstrance officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, he was transferred to remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，詔太子監國，太子稍嗜聲色，興土功。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era an edict ordered the crown prince to oversee the state; the crown prince gradually became fond of music and women and launched earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yifeng era an edict ordered the crown prince to oversee the state. The crown prince gradually became fond of music and women and launched earthworks.

sentences.zh: 承慶見造作玩好浮廣，倡優鼓吹讙嘩，戶奴小人皆得親左右、承顏色，恐因是作威福，宜加繩察，乃上疏極陳其端，又進《諭善箴》，太子頗嘉納。

translations.literal: Chengqing saw the construction of ornaments and curios growing extravagant, actors and musicians making clamor, household slaves and petty men all gaining access to his left and right and reading his expression; he feared they would thereby wield authority and blessings and that restraint should be added; he therefore submitted a memorial stating the full case and also presented Admonition on Goodness; the crown prince largely approved and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing saw extravagant construction of ornaments and curios, actors and musicians making clamor, and household slaves and petty men gaining access to the heir's side and reading his moods. He feared they would thereby wield power and demanded tighter restraint. He submitted a memorial stating the full case and also presented Admonition on Goodness; the crown prince largely approved and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 承慶嘗謂人所以擾濁浮躁，本之於心，乃著《靈臺賦》，譏揣當世，亦自廣其志。

translations.literal: Chengqing once said that what makes people turbulent, turbid, and restless has its root in the heart; he therefore wrote The Spirit Terrace Rhapsody, satirizing and probing the age, also to broaden his own purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing once said that what makes people turbulent and restless has its root in the heart. He therefore wrote The Spirit Terrace Rhapsody, satirizing the age and broadening his own purpose.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，出為烏程令。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, he was sent out as magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, he was sent out as magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷鳳閣舍人，掌天官選。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Phoenix Pavilion drafter with charge of the Bureau of Personnel selections.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Phoenix Pavilion drafter with charge of personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 屬文敏無留思，雖大詔令，未嘗著槁。

translations.literal: His literary composition was quick without lingering thought; even great edicts he never drafted in advance.
translations.idiomatic: His literary composition was quick without lingering thought; even great edicts he never drafted in advance.

sentences.zh: 失大臣意，出為沂州刺史。

translations.literal: He lost the chief ministers' favor and was sent out as prefect of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He lost the chief ministers' favor and was sent out as prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 明堂災，上疏諫，以「文明、垂拱後，執政者未滿歲，率以罪去，大抵皆惡逆不道。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall burned he submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: 'After the Wénmíng and Chuigong eras, those who held power had not completed a year before they were removed for crimes—mostly for wicked rebellion and unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall burned he submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, 'After the Wénmíng and Chuigong eras, those who held power had not completed a year before they were removed for crimes—mostly for wicked rebellion and unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 夫構大廈，濟巨川，必擇文梓、艅艎。

translations.literal: To build a great hall or cross a great river one must choose fine catalpa and large warships.
translations.idiomatic: To build a great hall or cross a great river one must choose fine catalpa timber and large warships.

sentences.zh: 若亟毀而敗，則是庇朽木、乘膠船也。

translations.literal: If one hastily destroys and fails, it is to shelter rotten wood and ride a glue boat.
translations.idiomatic: If one hastily destroys and fails, it is to shelter rotten wood and ride a glue boat.

sentences.zh: 臣謂陛下求賢之意切，而取人之路寬，故一言有合，而付大任。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that Your Majesty's intent to seek the worthy is keen, yet the path of selecting men is broad; therefore one phrase that fits and great responsibility is entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Your Majesty's intent to seek the worthy is keen, yet the path of selecting men is too broad; therefore one phrase that fits and great responsibility is entrusted.

sentences.zh: 夫以堯舉舜，猶歷試諸難，況庸庸者可超處輔相，以百揆萬機畀小人哉？」

translations.literal: When Yao raised Shun he still tested him through many hardships—how much less can the mediocre leap to the position of chief minister and have the hundred affairs and myriad mechanisms entrusted to petty men?'
translations.idiomatic: When Yao raised Shun he still tested him through many hardships—how much less can the mediocre leap to chief minister and have the hundred affairs and myriad mechanisms of state entrusted to petty men?'

sentences.zh: 書聞不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was received but no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received but no reply was given.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為舍人，掌選。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made drafter with charge of selections.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made drafter with charge of selections.

sentences.zh: 病免，改太子諭德。

translations.literal: Illness led to his dismissal; he was changed to the crown prince's moral instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led to his dismissal; he was changed to the crown prince's moral instructor.

sentences.zh: 歷豫、虢二州刺史，有善政。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Yu and Guo and had good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Yu and Guo and earned a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 轉天官侍郎，修國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Bureau of Personnel and edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the Bureau of Personnel and edited the national history.

sentences.zh: 凡三掌選，銓授平允，議者公之。

translations.literal: In all he thrice held charge of selections; his appointments were fair and even, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In all he thrice held charge of selections; his appointments were fair and even, and commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 長安中，拜鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era he was appointed vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an era he was appointed vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 張易之誅，承慶以素附離，免冠待罪。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi was executed, Chengqing because he had long been attached to him removed his cap and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yizhi was executed, Chengqing, because he had long been attached to him, removed his cap and awaited punishment.

sentences.zh: 時議草赦令，咸推承慶，召使為之，無橈色誤辭，援筆而就，眾嘆其壯。

translations.literal: At the time in drafting the amnesty edict all recommended Chengqing; he was summoned to compose it without a bent expression or mistaken phrase; he took up the brush and finished; the crowd admired his fortitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the court drafted the amnesty edict all recommended Chengqing. He was summoned to compose it without a bent expression or mistaken phrase, took up the brush and finished at once, and the crowd admired his fortitude.

sentences.zh: 然以累猶流嶺表。

translations.literal: Yet because of his connections he was still exiled beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of his connections he was still exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜辰州刺史，未行，以秘書員外少監召，兼脩國史，封扶陽縣子。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed prefect of Chen; before he departed he was summoned as acting deputy director of the Secretariat and concurrently to edit the national history, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed prefect of Chen. Before he could depart he was summoned as acting deputy director of the Secretariat to edit the national history concurrently and enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 詔撰《武后紀聖文》，中宗善之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to compose Record of the Sage Empress Wu; Emperor Zhongzong approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to compose Record of the Sage Empress Wu; Emperor Zhongzong approved the work.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Yellow Gate but before he took office he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the Yellow Gate but died before he could take office.

sentences.zh: 帝悼之，召其弟相州刺史嗣立會葬，因拜黃門侍郎繼其位。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him, summoned his younger brother Silin, prefect of Xiang, to attend the funeral, and thereupon appointed him vice minister of the Yellow Gate to succeed his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, summoned his younger brother Silin, prefect of Xiang, to attend the funeral, and thereupon appointed Silin vice minister of the Yellow Gate to succeed his post.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚曰溫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made minister of rites, posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed minister of rites, with the posthumous name Wen (Gentle).

sentences.zh: 嗣立，字延構，與承慶異母。

translations.literal: Silin, courtesy name Yangou, was a half-brother of Chengqing.
translations.idiomatic: Silin, styled Yangou, was Chengqing's half-brother.

sentences.zh: 少友悌，母遇承慶嚴，每笞，輒解衣求代，母不聽，即遣奴自捶，母感寤，為均愛。

translations.literal: From youth he was friendly and deferential to his elder brother; his mother treated Chengqing harshly and whenever she beat him he would remove his clothes and beg to take his place; when his mother would not listen he sent a slave to beat himself; his mother was moved to awakening and treated them with equal love.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was friendly and deferential to his elder brother. His mother treated Chengqing harshly, and whenever she beat him Silin would remove his clothes and beg to take the punishment. When his mother would not listen he sent a slave to beat him instead. His mother was moved and thereafter treated them with equal love.

sentences.zh: 世比晉王覽。

translations.literal: The age compared him to Wang Lan of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries compared him to Wang Lan of Jin.

sentences.zh: 第進士，累調雙流令，政為二川最。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination, was repeatedly assigned as magistrate of Shuangliu, and his governance was the best in the two Sichuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the jinshi examination, was repeatedly assigned as magistrate of Shuangliu, and his governance was ranked the best in the two Sichuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 承慶解鳳閣舍人，武后召嗣立謂曰：「爾父嘗稱二子忠且孝，堪事朕。

translations.literal: When Chengqing resigned as Phoenix Pavilion drafter, Empress Wu summoned Silin and said: 'Your father once praised you two brothers as loyal and filial, fit to serve Us.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqing resigned as Phoenix Pavilion drafter, Empress Wu summoned Silin and said, 'Your father once praised you two brothers as loyal and filial, fit to serve me.

sentences.zh: 比兄弟稱職，如而父言。

translations.literal: Recently you brothers have performed your duties well, as your father said.
translations.idiomatic: Recently you brothers have performed your duties well, as your father said.

sentences.zh: 今使卿兄弟自相代。」

translations.literal: Now I shall have you brothers replace each other.'
translations.idiomatic: Now I shall have you brothers replace each other.'

sentences.zh: 即拜鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Phoenix Pavilion drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed Phoenix Pavilion drafter.

sentences.zh: 時學校廢，刑濫及善人，乃上書極陳：「永淳後，庠序隳散，胄子衰缺，儒學之官輕，章句之選弛。

translations.literal: At the time schools were abandoned and punishments spread to the good; he therefore submitted a memorial stating fully: 'After Yongchun, the academies fell apart, the noble scions declined and were lacking, the offices of Confucian learning were slighted, and the selection of classical commentators was lax.
translations.idiomatic: At the time schools were abandoned and punishments spread to the innocent. He submitted a memorial stating fully: 'After Yongchun the academies fell apart, noble scions declined, the offices of Confucian learning were slighted, and the selection of classical commentators was lax.

sentences.zh: 貴閥後生以僥幸升，寒族平流以替業去。

translations.literal: Young men of noble clans rose by luck, while common families of plain standing left their trades.
translations.idiomatic: Young men of noble clans rose by luck, while common families of plain standing abandoned their proper trades.

sentences.zh: 垂拱間，仕入彌多，公行私謁，選補逾濫；

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era entrants to office grew ever more numerous, public conduct was private solicitation, and appointments grew ever more excessive;
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuigong era entrants to office grew ever more numerous, public conduct gave way to private solicitation, and appointments grew ever more excessive;

sentences.zh: 經術不聞，猛暴相誇。

translations.literal: classical learning was unheard, and the fierce and violent boasted to one another.
translations.idiomatic: classical learning was unheard, and the fierce and violent boasted to one another.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠下明詔，追三館生徒，敕王公以下子弟一入太學，尊尚師儒，發揚勸獎，海內知向。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would truly issue a clear edict, recall the students of the three halls, order the sons and younger brothers of princes and dukes down to enter the Imperial Academy, honor teachers and Confucians, extend encouragement and rewards, all within the seas would know where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would truly issue a clear edict, recall the students of the three halls, order the sons and younger brothers of princes and dukes down to enter the Imperial Academy, honor teachers and Confucians, extend encouragement and rewards, all within the seas would know where to turn.

sentences.zh: 然後審畀銓總，各程所能。

translations.literal: Then examine and assign the selections chief, each graded by ability.
translations.idiomatic: Then examine and assign the selections chief, each candidate graded by ability.

sentences.zh: 以之臨人，則官無曠，民樂業矣。」

translations.literal: With this to govern the people, then offices would have no vacancies and the people would rejoice in their occupations.'
translations.idiomatic: With this to govern the people, offices would have no vacancies and the people would rejoice in their occupations.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「揚豫以來，大獄屢興，窮治連捕，數年不絕。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Since Yang and Yu, great prisons have repeatedly arisen, exhaustive investigation and chained arrests continuing for years without end.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, 'Since the Yang and Yu affairs, great prisons have repeatedly arisen, with exhaustive investigation and chained arrests continuing for years without end.

sentences.zh: 大猾伺間，陰相影會，構似是之言，正不赥之辜，恣行楚慘，類自誣服，王公士人，至連頸就戮。

translations.literal: Great villains watched for openings and secretly joined in shadowy conspiracy, fabricating seemingly plausible words and fixing guilt on the guiltless, wantonly applying cruel torture until victims falsely confessed; princes, dukes, gentlemen, and scholars were led in chains to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Great villains watched for openings and secretly joined in shadowy conspiracy, fabricating seemingly plausible charges and fixing guilt on the innocent, wantonly applying cruel torture until victims falsely confessed. Princes, dukes, gentlemen, and scholars were led in chains to execution.

sentences.zh: 道路藉藉，咸知其非，而鍛練已成，不可翻動。

translations.literal: On the roads there was widespread talk; all knew it was wrong, yet the forged cases were already complete and could not be overturned.
translations.idiomatic: On the roads there was widespread talk; all knew it was wrong, yet the forged cases were already complete and could not be overturned.

sentences.zh: 小則身誅，大則族夷，相緣共坐者庸可勝道？

translations.literal: In small cases the body was executed, in great cases the clan was exterminated—those implicated and punished together, how could they be fully told?
translations.idiomatic: In small cases the body was executed; in great cases the clan was exterminated. Those implicated and punished together—who could count them all?

sentences.zh: 彼皆報讎復嫌，茍圖功求官賞耳。

translations.literal: They were all repaying grudges and settling suspicions, merely scheming for merit and seeking official rewards.
translations.idiomatic: They were all repaying grudges and settling suspicions, merely scheming for merit and seeking official rewards.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下廓天地之施、雷雨之仁，取垂拱以來罪無重輕所不赦者，普皆原洗。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty would broaden Heaven-and-Earth's grace and thunder-and-rain's benevolence, taking all since Chuigong whose crimes of whatever weight were not pardoned and universally restoring and washing them clean.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty would broaden Heaven-and-Earth's grace and thunder-and-rain's benevolence, taking all since the Chuigong era whose crimes of whatever weight were not pardoned and universally restoring and washing them clean.

sentences.zh: 死者還官，生者沾恩，則天下瞭然，知向所陷罪，非陛下意也。」

translations.literal: The dead would have offices restored, the living would receive grace, and all under Heaven would clearly know that the crimes into which they had been trapped were not Your Majesty's intent.'
translations.idiomatic: The dead would have offices restored, the living would receive grace, and all under Heaven would clearly know that the crimes into which they had been trapped were not Your Majesty's intent.'

sentences.zh: 長安中，拜鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era he was appointed vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an era he was appointed vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 時州縣非其人，後以為憂。

translations.literal: At the time prefectures and counties lacked the right men, and the empress later took this as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time prefectures and counties lacked the right men, and the empress later took this as a worry.

sentences.zh: 李嶠、唐休璟曰：「今朝廷重內官，輕外職，每除牧守，皆訴不行，非過累不得遣。

translations.literal: Li Qiao and Tang Xiujing said: 'Now the court values inner offices and slight outer posts; whenever a prefect or governor is appointed, all plead that they cannot go—not unless they have many faults can they be sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiao and Tang Xiujing said, 'Now the court values inner offices and slight outer posts. Whenever a prefect or governor is appointed, all plead that they cannot go—not unless they have many faults can they be sent out.

sentences.zh: 請撰臺閣賢者分典大州，自近臣始。」

translations.literal: Please select worthy men from the terrace and pavilion offices to administer great prefectures, beginning with near ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: Please select worthy men from the terrace and pavilion offices to administer great prefectures, beginning with near ministers.'

sentences.zh: 後曰：「誰為朕行？」

translations.literal: The empress said: 'Who will go for Us?'
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, 'Who will go for me?'

sentences.zh: 嗣立曰：「內典機要，非臣所堪，請先行以示群臣。」

translations.literal: Silin said: 'Inner governance of secrets is not what your subject can bear; please let your subject go first to show the ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: Silin said, 'Inner governance of secrets is not what I can bear; please let me go first to show the ministers.'

sentences.zh: 後悅，以本官檢校汴州刺史，由是左肅政大夫楊再思等十八人悉補外。

translations.literal: The empress was pleased and sent him out with his present office as acting prefect of Bian; thereupon the left rectifier-in-chief Yang Zaisi and eighteen others were all posted outside.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was pleased and sent him out with his present office as acting prefect of Bian. Thereupon the left rectifier-in-chief Yang Zaisi and eighteen others were all posted outside.

sentences.zh: 未幾，承慶知政事，嗣立以成均祭酒徙魏、洺二州，政無它異。

translations.literal: Before long Chengqing entered the administration; Silin was moved from director of the Imperial College to Wei and Ming prefectures, and his governance had no other peculiarity.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chengqing entered the administration. Silin was moved from director of the Imperial College to Wei and Ming prefectures, and his governance had no other peculiarity.

sentences.zh: 坐善二張，貶饒州長史。

translations.literal: Punished for associating with the two Zhangs, he was demoted to chief administrator of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for associating with the two Zhang brothers, he was demoted to chief administrator of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 繇相州刺史入為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: From prefect of Xiang he entered court as vice minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: From prefect of Xiang he entered court as vice minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 轉太府卿、修文館大學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of the granaries and grand academician of the Xiuxuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of the granaries and grand academician of the Xiuxuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 中宗景龍中，拜兵部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era of Zhongzong he was appointed minister of war and third rank with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong era of Zhongzong he was appointed minister of war and third rank with the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時崇飾觀寺，用度百出。

translations.literal: At the time they lavishly adorned temples and shrines, and expenditures issued in a hundred directions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they lavishly adorned temples and shrines, and expenditures issued in a hundred directions.

sentences.zh: 又恩幸食邑者眾，封戶凡五十四州，皆據天下上腴。

translations.literal: Those granted fief sustenance by favor were numerous; fief households totaled fifty-four prefectures, all occupying the empire's richest lands.
translations.idiomatic: Those granted fief sustenance by favor were numerous; fief households totaled fifty-four prefectures, all occupying the empire's richest lands.

sentences.zh: 一封分食數州，隨土所宜，牟取利入。

translations.literal: One fief divided its sustenance among several prefectures, taking profit according to whatever each region offered.
translations.idiomatic: One fief divided its sustenance among several prefectures, taking profit according to whatever each region offered.

sentences.zh: 至安樂、太平公主，率取高貲多丁家，無復如平民有所損免，為封戶者亟於軍興。

translations.literal: Down to Princess Anle and Princess Taiping, they mostly chose wealthy households with many adult males, so that commoners no longer received exemptions and reductions as before, and those serving as fief households were pressed like wartime levies.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Princess Anle and Princess Taiping, they mostly chose wealthy households with many adult males, so that commoners no longer received exemptions and reductions as before, and those serving as fief households were pressed like wartime levies.

sentences.zh: 監察御史宋務光建言：「願停徵封，一切附租庸輸送。」

translations.literal: The investigating censor Song Wuguang proposed: 'I wish the collection of fief dues be stopped and all be attached to the equal tax and corvée deliveries.'
translations.idiomatic: The investigating censor Song Wuguang proposed, 'I wish the collection of fief dues be stopped and all be attached to the equal tax and corvée deliveries.'

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: It was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 嗣立建言：

translations.literal: Silin proposed:
translations.idiomatic: Silin proposed:

sentences.zh: 今稟帑耗竭，無一歲之儲。

translations.literal: Now the treasury stores are exhausted and there is not one year's reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Now the treasury stores are exhausted and there is not one year's reserve.

sentences.zh: 假遇水旱，人須賑給，不時軍興，士待資裝，陛下何以具之？

translations.literal: If flood or drought come, the people will need relief; if war arises without warning, soldiers will need supplies—how will Your Majesty provide them?
translations.idiomatic: If flood or drought come, the people will need relief; if war arises without warning, soldiers will need supplies—how will Your Majesty provide them?

sentences.zh: 伏見營立寺觀，累年不絕，鴻侈繁麗，務相矜勝，大抵費常千萬以上。

translations.literal: I see the construction of temples and shrines continuing year after year without cease, vast and ornate, each striving to outdo the other—altogether costing more than ten million on the usual scale.
translations.idiomatic: I see the construction of temples and shrines continuing year after year without cease, vast and ornate, each striving to outdo the other—altogether costing more than ten million on the usual scale.

sentences.zh: 轉徙木石，廢功害農；

translations.literal: Timber and stone are moved about, wasting labor and harming agriculture;
translations.idiomatic: Timber and stone are moved about, wasting labor and harming agriculture;

sentences.zh: 地藏開發，蟄蟲傷露。

translations.literal: the earth is opened and hibernating creatures are harmed by the dew.
translations.idiomatic: the earth is opened and hibernating creatures are harmed by the dew.

sentences.zh: 上聖至慈，理必不然。

translations.literal: The most sagely and supremely benevolent—by principle this surely cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: The most sagely and supremely benevolent—by principle this surely cannot be.

sentences.zh: 準之道法則乖，質之生人則損。

translations.literal: Measured against the Way and its methods it is wrong; weighed against the living it is harmful.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the Way and its methods it is wrong; weighed against the living it is harmful.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈不是思？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty not reflect on this?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty not reflect on this?

sentences.zh: 又食封之家，日月猥眾，凡用戶部丁六十萬，人課二絹，則固一百二十萬。

translations.literal: Again, households with fief sustenance grow daily in number; in all they use six hundred thousand adult males from the Ministry of Revenue registers, two bolts of silk per man, which is fixed at one million two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Again, households with fief sustenance grow daily in number; in all they use six hundred thousand adult males from the Ministry of Revenue registers, two bolts of silk per man, which is fixed at one million two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 臣見太府歲調絹才百萬匹，少則十之二，有所貸免，曾不半在。

translations.literal: I see the Grand Treasury each year requisitions only one million bolts of silk, sometimes as little as two tenths, with loans and exemptions—never even half remains.
translations.idiomatic: I see the Grand Treasury each year requisitions only one million bolts of silk, sometimes as little as two tenths, with loans and exemptions—never even half remains.

sentences.zh: 比諸封家，所入已寡。

translations.literal: Compared with fief households, what enters the state is already scant.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with fief households, what enters the state is already scant.

sentences.zh: 國初功臣，共定天下，食封不三十家，今橫恩特賜，家至百四十以上。

translations.literal: At the dynasty's founding the meritorious ministers together settled the realm; those with fief sustenance were fewer than thirty households. Now favor is bestowed broadly and households reach more than one hundred forty.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding the meritorious ministers together settled the realm; those with fief sustenance were fewer than thirty households. Now favor is bestowed broadly and households reach more than one hundred forty.

sentences.zh: 天下租賦，在公不足，而私有餘。

translations.literal: The empire's land tax and corvée—what belongs to the public is insufficient while the private has surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's land tax and corvée—what belongs to the public is insufficient while the private has surplus.

sentences.zh: 又封家徵求，各遣奴皂，淩突侵漁，百姓怨嘆。

translations.literal: Again fief households in collecting dues each send slave runners who bully and encroach, and the people groan in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Again fief households in collecting dues each send slave runners who bully and encroach, and the people groan in resentment.

sentences.zh: 或貿易斷盜，誅責紛紜，曾無少息。

translations.literal: Some trade by force or steal outright; punishments and demands fly in confusion without the slightest pause.
translations.idiomatic: Some trade by force or steal outright; punishments and demands fly in confusion without the slightest pause.

sentences.zh: 下民窶乏，何以堪命？

translations.literal: The lower people are impoverished—how can they bear such exactions?
translations.idiomatic: The lower people are impoverished—how can they bear such exactions?

sentences.zh: 臣願以丁課一送太府，封家詣左藏仰給，禁止自徵，以息重困。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes the adult-male silk tax be sent once to the Grand Treasury, fief households to receive allotments from the left vault on presentation, and private collection forbidden, to ease this crushing burden.
translations.idiomatic: I wish the adult-male silk tax be sent once to the Grand Treasury, fief households to receive allotments from the left vault on presentation, and private collection forbidden, to ease this crushing burden.
