sentences.zh: 臣聞設官建吏，本於治人而務安之也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that establishing offices and appointing clerks has its root in governing people and making them secure.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that establishing offices and appointing clerks has its root in governing people and making them secure.

sentences.zh: 明官得其人，則天下治。

translations.literal: When enlightened offices obtain the right men, then the realm is governed.
translations.idiomatic: When enlightened offices obtain the right men, then the realm is governed.

sentences.zh: 古者取士，先鄉曲之譽，然後辟於州；

translations.literal: In antiquity in taking scholars, one first sought village reputation, then recruited them in the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity in taking scholars, one first sought village reputation, then recruited them in the prefecture;

sentences.zh: 州已試，然後辟五府；

translations.literal: after the prefecture had tested them, then recruited them in the five bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: after the prefecture had tested them, then recruited them in the five bureaus;

sentences.zh: 五府著聞，乃升諸朝。

translations.literal: when their fame was established in the five bureaus, then they were raised to court.
translations.idiomatic: when their fame was established in the five bureaus, then they were raised to court.

sentences.zh: 得不謂所擇悉而所歷深乎？

translations.literal: Can one say that what was chosen was thorough and what was experienced was deep?
translations.idiomatic: Can one say that what was chosen was thorough and what was experienced was deep?

sentences.zh: 今之取人，未試而遽遷，務進僥幸，比肩系踵。

translations.literal: In taking men today, before trial they are hurriedly transferred, striving for advancement by luck, shoulder to shoulder in endless succession.
translations.idiomatic: In taking men today, before trial they are hurriedly transferred, striving for advancement by luck, shoulder to shoulder in endless succession.

sentences.zh: 故文者治官，則回邪贓汙；

translations.literal: Therefore when literary men govern offices, they are crooked, evil, and filthy;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when literary men govern offices, they are crooked, evil, and filthy;

sentences.zh: 武者治軍，則庸懦怯弱。

translations.literal: when military men govern armies, they are mediocre, weak, and cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: when military men govern armies, they are mediocre, weak, and cowardly.

sentences.zh: 補授亡限，員外置官，吏困供承，官竭資奉。

translations.literal: Supplementary appointments have no limit, supernumerary offices are set up, clerks are exhausted supplying them, and offices are drained of salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Supplementary appointments have no limit, supernumerary offices are set up, clerks are exhausted supplying them, and offices are drained of salaries.

sentences.zh: 國家大事，豈甚於此？

translations.literal: Are state great affairs more serious than this?
translations.idiomatic: Are state great affairs more serious than this?

sentences.zh: 古者，設爵待士，才者有之。

translations.literal: In antiquity ranks were set to await scholars; the talented received them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity ranks were set to await scholars; the talented received them.

sentences.zh: 不才者進，則有才之路塞。

translations.literal: When the untalented advance, the path for the talented is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: When the untalented advance, the path for the talented is blocked.

sentences.zh: 賢人據正，遠僥幸之門。

translations.literal: The worthy hold the upright and keep far the gate of luck.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy hold the upright and keep far the gate of luck.

sentences.zh: 僥幸開，則賢者隱矣。

translations.literal: When the gate of luck opens, the worthy withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the gate of luck opens, the worthy withdraw.

sentences.zh: 賢者隱，則人不安；

translations.literal: When the worthy withdraw, then people are not secure;
translations.idiomatic: When the worthy withdraw, then people are not secure;

sentences.zh: 人不安，國將危矣。

translations.literal: when people are not secure, the state will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: when people are not secure, the state will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 刺史、縣令，治人之首，比年不加簡擇，京官坐負及聲稱下者乃典州，吏部年高不善刀筆者乃擬縣。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates are the heads of governing people; in recent years they have not been carefully chosen—capital officials who sit in debt or whose reputation is low are made to administer prefectures, and Ministry of Revenue men who are old and poor at documents are assigned to counties.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates are the heads of governing people; in recent years they have not been carefully chosen—capital officials who sit in debt or whose reputation is low are made to administer prefectures, and Ministry of Revenue men who are old and poor at documents are assigned to counties.

sentences.zh: 朝輕用人，何以治國？

translations.literal: If the court lightly uses men, how can it govern the state?
translations.idiomatic: If the court lightly uses men, how can it govern the state?

sentences.zh: 願下有司，精加汰擇。

translations.literal: I wish that subordinate offices be ordered to refine and select carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that subordinate offices be ordered to refine and select carefully.

sentences.zh: 凡諸曹侍郎、兩省、二臺及五品以上清望官，當先選用刺史、縣令，所冀守宰稱職，以興太平。

translations.literal: All vice ministers of the various bureaus, both secretariats, both censorates, and clear-reputation officials of fifth rank and above should first be chosen as prefects and magistrates, so that prefects and magistrates may perform their duties and great peace arise.
translations.idiomatic: All vice ministers of the various bureaus, both secretariats, both censorates, and clear-reputation officials of fifth rank and above should first be chosen as prefects and magistrates, so that prefects and magistrates may perform their duties and great peace arise.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 嗣立與韋后屬疏，帝特詔附屬籍，顧待甚渥。

translations.literal: Silin was distantly related to Empress Wei; the emperor specially ordered him attached to her clan register and treated him with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Silin was distantly related to Empress Wei; the emperor specially ordered him attached to her clan register and treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 營別第驪山鸚鵡谷，帝臨幸，命從官賦詩，制序冠篇，賜況優備，因封嗣立逍遙公，名所居曰清虛原幽棲谷。

translations.literal: He built a separate mansion in the Parrot Valley at Mount Li; when the emperor visited, he ordered his followers to compose poems and placed his preface at the head; the gifts and favors were complete, and he enfeoffed Silin as Duke of Xiaoyao, naming his residence Clear Void Plain and Secluded Dwelling Valley.
translations.idiomatic: He built a separate mansion in the Parrot Valley at Mount Li. When the emperor visited, he ordered his followers to compose poems and placed his preface at the head. The gifts and favors were complete, and he enfeoffed Silin as Duke of Xiaoyao, naming his residence Clear Void Plain and Secluded Dwelling Valley.

sentences.zh: 嗣立獻木杯、藤盤數十物。

translations.literal: Silin presented several dozen wooden cups and rattan trays.
translations.idiomatic: Silin presented several dozen wooden cups and rattan trays.

sentences.zh: 唐隆初，拜中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tanglong era he was appointed chief minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tanglong era he was appointed chief minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 韋后敗，幾死於亂，寧王為救免。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei was defeated he nearly died in the turmoil; the Prince of Ning saved him and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei was defeated he nearly died in the turmoil; the Prince of Ning saved him and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 出為許州刺史，以定策立睿宗，賜封百戶，徙汝州。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Xu; because he helped establish the decisive policy that made Ruizong emperor, he was granted one hundred fief households and was moved to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Xu. Because he helped establish the decisive policy that made Ruizong emperor, he was granted one hundred fief households and was moved to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為國子祭酒、太子賓客。

translations.literal: He entered court as director of the Imperial College and companion to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as director of the Imperial College and companion to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 坐宗楚客等削遺制事，不執正，貶岳州別駕。

translations.literal: Punished for joining Zong Chuke and others in tampering with the late emperor's will and not holding to what was right, he was demoted to assistant prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for joining Zong Chuke and others in tampering with the late emperor's will and not holding to what was right, he was demoted to assistant prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 再徙為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: He was moved again to prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved again to prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 開元中，河南道巡察使表其廉，欲復用，會卒，年六十六，贈兵部尚書，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era the Henan circuit inspection commissioner memorialized his integrity and wished to reuse him, but he died on the verge, age sixty-six; he was posthumously made minister of war, posthumous name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era the Henan circuit inspection commissioner memorialized his integrity and wished to reuse him, but he died on the verge, age sixty-six. He was posthumously appointed minister of war, with the posthumous name Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 初，嗣立代承慶為鳳閣舍人、黃門侍郎；

translations.literal: At first Silin replaced Chengqing as Phoenix Pavilion drafter and vice minister of the Yellow Gate;
translations.idiomatic: At first Silin replaced Chengqing as Phoenix Pavilion drafter and vice minister of the Yellow Gate;

sentences.zh: 承慶亦代為天官侍郎及知政事。

translations.literal: Chengqing also replaced him as vice minister of the Bureau of Personnel and in governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing also replaced him as vice minister of the Bureau of Personnel and in governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 父子並為宰相，世罕其比。

translations.literal: Father and son both served as chief ministers—a rarity in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both served as chief ministers—a rarity in the age.

sentences.zh: 有二子恒、濟，知名。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Heng and Ji, who were well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Heng and Ji, who were well known.

sentences.zh: 恒，開元初為碭山令，政寬惠，吏民愛之。

translations.literal: Heng, early in Kaiyuan, was magistrate of Dangshan; his governance was lenient and kind and clerks and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, early in Kaiyuan, was magistrate of Dangshan; his governance was lenient and kind and clerks and people loved him.

sentences.zh: 天子東巡，州縣供張，皆鞭撲趣辦，恒不立威而事給。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven toured the east, prefectures and counties supplied provisions; all used the whip to hurry completion, but Heng established no harsh authority yet everything was provided.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven toured the east, prefectures and counties supplied provisions; all used the whip to hurry completion, but Heng established no harsh authority yet everything was provided.

sentences.zh: 姑子御史中丞宇文融薦恒有經濟才，讓以其位，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His nephew by marriage, the censor-in-chief Yuwen Rong, recommended Heng for economic talent and yielded his own post; Heng was promoted to palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew by marriage, the censor-in-chief Yuwen Rong, recommended Heng for economic talent and yielded his own post; Heng was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 累轉給事中，為隴右、河西黜陟使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to drafting officer and made inspection commissioner for Longyou and Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred to drafting officer and made inspection commissioner for Longyou and Hexi.

sentences.zh: 時河西節度使蓋嘉運恃左右援，橫恣不法，妄列功狀，恒劾奏之，人代其恐，出為陳留太守，卒。

translations.literal: At the time the Hexi military governor Gai Jiayun relied on support from the inner court, acted lawlessly and arrogantly, and falsely listed merit records; Heng memorialized impeaching him; people took his place in fearing for him; he was sent out as prefect of Chenliu and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Hexi military governor Gai Jiayun relied on support from the inner court, acted lawlessly and arrogantly, and falsely listed merit records. Heng memorialized impeaching him; people feared for him in his place; he was sent out as prefect of Chenliu and died.

sentences.zh: 濟，開元初調鄄城令。

translations.literal: Ji, early in Kaiyuan, was assigned magistrate of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, early in Kaiyuan, was assigned magistrate of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 或言吏部選縣令非其人，既眾謝，有詔問所以安人者，對凡二百人，惟濟居第一，不能對者悉免官。

translations.literal: Someone said the Ministry of Personnel's selection of magistrates was not the right men; after the mass apology, an edict asked how one secures the people; of two hundred respondents only Ji ranked first, and those who could not answer were all dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said the Ministry of Personnel's selection of magistrates was not the right men. After the mass apology, an edict asked how one secures the people; of two hundred respondents only Ji ranked first, and those who could not answer were all dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 於是擢濟醴泉令，侍郎盧從願、李朝隱並貶為刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ji was promoted to magistrate of Liquan, and vice ministers Lu Congyuan and Li Chaoyin were both demoted to prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ji was promoted to magistrate of Liquan, and vice ministers Lu Congyuan and Li Chaoyin were both demoted to prefects.

sentences.zh: 濟四遷戶部侍郎，為太原尹。

translations.literal: Ji was four times promoted to vice minister of revenue and made prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was four times promoted to vice minister of revenue and made prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 著《先德詩》四章，世服其典懿。

translations.literal: He wrote four chapters of Odes of Former Virtue, and the age admired their classical elegance.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote four chapters of Odes of Former Virtue, and the age admired their classical elegance.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，授尚書左丞，凡三世居之。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he was appointed left vice director of the secretariat; three generations of the family held the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he was appointed left vice director of the secretariat; three generations of the family held the post.

sentences.zh: 濟文雅，頗能脩飾政事，所至有治稱。

translations.literal: Ji was refined in letters and quite able to polish administrative affairs; wherever he went he earned praise for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was refined in letters and quite able to polish administrative affairs; wherever he went he earned praise for good governance.

sentences.zh: 終馮翊太守。

translations.literal: He ended as prefect of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as prefect of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 子奧，夏令，亦以能政聞。

translations.literal: His son Ao was magistrate of Xia and was also known for able governance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ao was magistrate of Xia and was also known for able governance.

sentences.zh: 嗣立孫弘景，擢進士第，數佐節度府。

translations.literal: Silin's grandson Hongjing passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly served on military governors' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Silin's grandson Hongjing passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly served on military governors' staffs.

sentences.zh: 以左補闕召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as left remonstrance officer and made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as left remonstrance officer and made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 蘇光榮為涇原節度使，弘景當草詔，書辭不如旨，罷學士。

translations.literal: When Su Guangrong was military governor of Jingyuan, Hongjing was to draft the edict; the wording did not please and he was dismissed from the academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Guangrong was military governor of Jingyuan, Hongjing was to draft the edict; the wording did not please and he was dismissed from the academy.

sentences.zh: 遷累度支郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 張仲方黜李進甫謚得罪，憲宗意弘景擿助，出為綿州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhongfang demoted Li Jinfu's posthumous title and was punished, Emperor Xianzong suspected Hongjing had helped expose him and sent him out as prefect of Mian.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhongfang demoted Li Jinfu's posthumous title and was punished, Emperor Xianzong suspected Hongjing had helped expose him and sent him out as prefect of Mian.

sentences.zh: 李夷簡鎮淮南，奏以自副。

translations.literal: Li Yijian governed Huainan and memorialized to have him as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yijian governed Huainan and memorialized to have him as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 召入，再遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was summoned in and twice promoted to drafting officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned in and twice promoted to drafting officer.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉劉士涇賂權近，擢太僕卿，弘景上還詔書，穆宗使喻：「其先人昌有功，朕所以念功睦親者。」

translations.literal: The imperial son-in-law Liu Shijing bribed those near power and was promoted to minister of imperial stud; Hongjing returned the edict to the throne; Emperor Muzong sent someone to explain: 'His forebear Chang had merit; it is for this that We think of merit and draw kin close.'
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son-in-law Liu Shijing bribed those near power and was promoted to minister of imperial stud. Hongjing returned the edict to the throne. Emperor Muzong sent someone to explain, 'His forebear Chang had merit; it is for this that I think of merit and draw kin close.'

sentences.zh: 弘景固執，帝怒，使宣慰安南。

translations.literal: Hongjing stood firm; the emperor was angry and sent him to announce peace in Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing stood firm; the emperor was angry and sent him to announce peace in Annan.

sentences.zh: 由是有名。

translations.literal: Thereby he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he became famous.

sentences.zh: 時蕭俯輔政，弘景議論常佐佑之。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Mian was chief minister; Hongjing's deliberations often assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiao Mian was chief minister; Hongjing's deliberations often assisted him.

sentences.zh: 還，再遷吏部侍郎，銓綜平序，貴幸憚其嚴，不敢郤以私。

translations.literal: On his return he was twice promoted to vice minister of the civil service; his selections were fair and orderly, and the powerful feared his severity and did not dare press him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was twice promoted to vice minister of the civil service; his selections were fair and orderly, and the powerful feared his severity and did not dare press him with private requests.

sentences.zh: 歷陜虢觀察使，召拜尚書左丞，駁正吏銓所除六十餘官不當進資，於是鄭絪、丁公著、楊嗣復皆奪俸，郎吏肅然，望風脩整。

translations.literal: He served as military governor of Shan, Guo, and Guan, was summoned as left vice director of the secretariat, and rejected more than sixty officials whom the Ministry of Personnel had promoted with improper advancement; thereupon Zheng Yin, Ding Gongzhu, and Yang Sifu all had salaries seized, and clerks grew orderly, mending conduct at the wind's approach.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military governor of Shan, Guo, and Guan, was summoned as left vice director of the secretariat, and rejected more than sixty officials whom the Ministry of Personnel had promoted improperly. Thereupon Zheng Yin, Ding Gongzhu, and Yang Sifu all had salaries seized, and the clerks grew orderly, mending conduct wherever his influence reached.

sentences.zh: 吏部員外郎楊虞卿以累下吏，詔弘景與御史詳讞。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel aide Yang Yuqing was repeatedly sent down to the law officers; an edict ordered Hongjing and the censors to examine the case in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel aide Yang Yuqing was repeatedly sent down to the law officers. An edict ordered Hongjing and the censors to examine the case in detail.

sentences.zh: 虞卿私造門，弘景厲言曰：「有詔按公，尚私謁邪？」

translations.literal: Yuqing privately came to his door; Hongjing spoke sternly: 'There is an edict to investigate you—do you still make private visits?'
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing came to his door privately. Hongjing spoke sternly, 'There is an edict to investigate you—do you still make private visits?'

sentences.zh: 虞卿多朋助，自謂必見納，及是，惶恐去。

translations.literal: Yuqing had many partisan helpers and believed he would surely be accepted; at this he departed in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing had many partisan helpers and believed he would surely be accepted. At this he departed in fear.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of rites and eastern capital defender.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of rites and eastern capital defender.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-six and was posthumously made left vice director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six and was posthumously appointed left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 弘景以直道進，議論持正有守，當時風教所倚賴，為長慶名卿。

translations.literal: Hongjing advanced by the upright path; his deliberations held to what was right and had constancy; at the time custom and teaching relied on him, and he was a famed minister of the Changqing era.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing advanced by the upright path. His deliberations held to what was right and had constancy. At the time custom and teaching relied on him, and he was a famed minister of the Changqing era.

sentences.zh: 陸元方，字希仲，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Lu Yuanfang, courtesy name Xizhong, was a native of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanfang, styled Xizhong, was a native of Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳給事黃門侍郎琛之曾孫。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Chen, drafting officer and vice director of the Yellow Gate Chen Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Chen Zhi, drafting officer and vice director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 伯父柬之，善書名家，官太子司議郎。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Dongzhi was skilled in calligraphy and a famous family; he served as remonstrance officer of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Dongzhi was skilled in calligraphy and a famous family name. He served as remonstrance officer of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 元方初明經，後舉八科皆中。

translations.literal: Yuanfang first passed the classics examination, then placed in all eight special examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang first passed the classics examination, then placed in all eight special examinations.

sentences.zh: 累轉監察御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 武后時，使嶺外，方涉海，風濤驚壯，舟人懼，元方曰：「吾受命不私，神豈害我？」

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu he was sent beyond the ranges; just as he was crossing the sea, wind and waves rose terrifyingly and the boatmen were afraid. Yuanfang said: 'I received my commission without private interest—would the spirits harm me?'
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he was sent beyond the ranges. Just as he was crossing the sea, wind and waves rose terrifyingly and the boatmen were afraid. Yuanfang said, 'I received my commission without private interest—would the spirits harm me?'

sentences.zh: 趣使濟，而風訖息。

translations.literal: He urged them on to cross, and the wind then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He urged them on to cross, and the wind then ceased.

sentences.zh: 使還，除殿中侍御史，擢鳳閣舍人、秋官侍郎。

translations.literal: On his return he was made palace attendant censor and promoted to Phoenix Pavilion drafter and vice minister of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made palace attendant censor and promoted to Phoenix Pavilion drafter and vice minister of the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 為來俊臣所陷，後置不罪。

translations.literal: He was framed by Lai Junchen; the empress set the matter aside without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was framed by Lai Junchen. The empress set the matter aside without punishment.

sentences.zh: 遷鸞臺侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Luan Terrace and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the Luan Terrace and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 坐附會李昭德，貶綏州刺史。

translations.literal: Punished for associating with Li Zhaode, he was demoted to prefect of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for associating with Li Zhaode, he was demoted to prefect of Sui.

sentences.zh: 擢天官侍郎，兼司衛卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Bureau of Personnel and concurrently director of the Bureau of Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of the Bureau of Personnel and concurrently director of the Bureau of Guards.

sentences.zh: 或言其薦引皆親黨，後怒，免官，令白衣領職。

translations.literal: Someone said his recommendations were all kin and partisans; the empress was angry, removed him from office, and ordered him to hold his post in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said his recommendations were all kin and partisans. The empress was angry, removed him from office, and ordered him to hold his post in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 元方薦人如初，後召讓之，對曰：「舉臣所知，不暇問讎黨。」

translations.literal: Yuanfang recommended people as before; the empress summoned and rebuked him; he replied: 'I recommend those your subject knows—I have no leisure to ask whether they are enemies or partisans.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang recommended people as before. The empress summoned and rebuked him. He replied, 'I recommend those I know—I have no leisure to ask whether they are enemies or partisans.'

sentences.zh: 又薦其友崔玄暐有宰相才。

translations.literal: He also recommended his friend Cui Xuanwei as having chief-minister talent.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended his friend Cui Xuanwei as having chief-minister talent.

sentences.zh: 後知無它，復拜鸞臺侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: The empress knew there was nothing else against him and again appointed him vice minister of the Luan Terrace and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress knew there was nothing else against him and again appointed him vice minister of the Luan Terrace and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 後嘗問外事，對曰：「臣備位宰相，大事當白奏，民間碎務，不敢以聞。」

translations.literal: The empress once asked about outside affairs; he replied: 'Your subject holds a chief-minister's post; great affairs should be reported in memorials. Petty popular matters your subject dare not report.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress once asked about outside affairs. He replied, 'I hold a chief-minister's post. Great affairs should be reported in memorials. Petty popular matters I dare not report.'

sentences.zh: 忤旨，下除太子右庶子。

translations.literal: This offended the edict; he was demoted to right guardian of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the edict. He was demoted to right guardian of the heir.

sentences.zh: 進文昌左丞，卒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to left assistant director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to left assistant director of the Secretariat and died.

sentences.zh: 元方素清慎，再執政，每進退群臣，後必先訪問，外秘莫知。

translations.literal: Yuanfang was by nature pure and cautious; twice he held the government; whenever he advanced or dismissed ministers the empress always consulted him first, and outsiders in secret did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang was by nature pure and cautious. Twice he held the government. Whenever he advanced or dismissed ministers the empress always consulted him first, and outsiders in secret did not know.

sentences.zh: 臨終，取奏稿焚之，曰：「吾陰德在人，後當有興者。」

translations.literal: At his end he took his memorial drafts and burned them, saying: 'I have hidden virtue among the people; later there will be those who rise.'
translations.idiomatic: At his end he took his memorial drafts and burned them, saying, 'I have hidden virtue among the people. Later there will be those who rise.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「吾當壽，但領選久，耗傷吾神。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'I should have lived long, but holding selections too long wore down my spirit.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said, 'I should have lived long, but holding selections too long wore down my spirit.'

sentences.zh: 有一柙，生平所緘鑰者，歿後，家人發之，乃前後詔敕。

translations.literal: There was a box he had sealed in life; after his death the family opened it and found only edicts and orders from before and after.
translations.idiomatic: There was a box he had sealed in life. After his death the family opened it and found only edicts and orders from before and after.

sentences.zh: 贈越州都督。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made military governor of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed military governor of Yue.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆美才，而象先、景倩、景融尤知名。

translations.literal: All his sons were talented, but Xiangxian, Jingqian, and Jingrong were especially renowned.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons were talented, but Xiangxian, Jingqian, and Jingrong were especially renowned.

sentences.zh: 象先器識沈邃，舉制科高第，為揚州參軍事。

translations.literal: Xiangxian was deep in capacity and insight; he placed high in the special examination and was made aide in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian was deep in capacity and insight. He placed high in the special examination and was made aide in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時吉頊與元方同為吏部侍郎，頊擢象先為洛陽尉，元方不肯當，頊曰：「為官擇人，豈以吏部子廢至公邪？」

translations.literal: At the time Ji Xu and Yuanfang both served as vice ministers of the Bureau of Personnel; Xu promoted Xiangxian as Luoyang bailiff; Yuanfang would not accept it. Xu said: 'In appointing officials one chooses men—how can one discard the utmost public good because he is the Ministry of Personnel's son?'
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ji Xu and Yuanfang both served as vice ministers of the Bureau of Personnel. Xu promoted Xiangxian as Luoyang bailiff; Yuanfang would not accept it. Xu said, 'In appointing officials one chooses men—how can one discard the utmost public good because he is the Ministry of Personnel's son?'

sentences.zh: 卒以授。

translations.literal: He finally granted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He finally granted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 俄遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 累授中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed vice minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，進同中書門下平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era he was advanced to co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery and supervised editing the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun era he was advanced to co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery and supervised editing the national history.

sentences.zh: 初，太平公主謀引崔湜為宰相，湜曰：「象先人望，宜幹樞近，若不者，湜敢辭。」

translations.literal: At first Princess Taiping plotted to bring Cui Shi in as chief minister; Shi said: 'Xiangxian has public esteem and should handle the pivot—if not, Shi dares decline.'
translations.idiomatic: At first Princess Taiping plotted to bring Cui Shi in as chief minister. Shi said, 'Xiangxian has public esteem and should handle the pivot. If not, I dare decline.'

sentences.zh: 主不得已為言之，遂並知政事。

translations.literal: The princess had no choice but to speak for him, and they then both held government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had no choice but to speak for him, and they then both held government affairs.

sentences.zh: 然其性恬靜寡欲，議論高簡，為時推向。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was tranquil with few desires; his deliberations were lofty and concise, and the age exalted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was tranquil with few desires. His deliberations were lofty and concise, and the age exalted him.

sentences.zh: 湜嘗曰：「陸公加於人一等。」

translations.literal: Shi once said: 'Lord Lu stands one grade above other men.
translations.idiomatic: Shi once said, 'Lord Lu stands one grade above other men.

sentences.zh: 公主既擅權，宰相爭附之，象先未嘗往謁；

translations.literal: The princess already monopolized power and the chief ministers vied to attach themselves to her; Xiangxian had never gone to call on her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess already monopolized power and the chief ministers vied to attach themselves to her. Xiangxian had never gone to call on her.

sentences.zh: 及謀逆，召宰相議，曰：「寧王長，不當廢嫡立庶。」

translations.literal: When they plotted rebellion the princess summoned the chief ministers to deliberate, saying: 'The Prince of Ning is the elder—one should not depose the legitimate heir to establish a lesser son.
translations.idiomatic: When they plotted rebellion the princess summoned the chief ministers to deliberate, saying, 'The Prince of Ning is the elder—one should not depose the legitimate heir to establish a lesser son.

sentences.zh: 象先曰：「帝得立，何也？」

translations.literal: Xiangxian said: 'How did the emperor gain the throne?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian said, 'How did the emperor gain the throne?'

sentences.zh: 主曰：「帝有一時功，今失德，安可不廢？」

translations.literal: The princess said: 'The emperor had merit for a time; now he has lost virtue—how can he not be deposed?'
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, 'The emperor had merit for a time. Now he has lost virtue—how can he not be deposed?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「立以功者，廢必以罪。

translations.literal: He replied: 'Those established by merit are deposed only by crime.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'Those established by merit are deposed only by crime.

sentences.zh: 今不聞天子過失，安得廢？」

translations.literal: Now we do not hear of the Son of Heaven's faults—how can he be deposed?'
translations.idiomatic: Now we do not hear of the Son of Heaven's faults—how can he be deposed?'

sentences.zh: 主怒，更與竇懷貞等謀，卒誅死。

translations.literal: The princess was angry and plotted further with Dou Huaizhen and others; in the end she was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was angry and plotted further with Dou Huaizhen and others. In the end she was executed.

sentences.zh: 時象先與蕭至忠、岑羲等坐為主所進，將同誅，玄宗遽召免之，曰：「歲寒然後知松柏之後雕也！」

translations.literal: At the time Xiangxian, with Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others, sat in guilt as those the princess had advanced and were about to be executed together; Xuanzong urgently summoned and exempted him, saying: 'Only in cold years does one know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither!'
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiangxian, with Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others, sat in guilt as those the princess had advanced and were about to be executed together. Xuanzong urgently summoned and exempted him, saying, 'Only in cold years does one know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither!'

sentences.zh: 以保護功，封兗國公，賜封戶二百。

translations.literal: For the merit of protecting him he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan and granted two hundred fief households.
translations.idiomatic: For the merit of protecting him he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan and granted two hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 初，難作，睿宗禦承天樓，群臣稍集，帝麾曰：「助朕者留，不者去！」

translations.literal: At first, when the crisis arose, Ruizong mounted the Chengtian Tower; as ministers gradually gathered, the emperor waved and said: 'Those who help Us stay; those who do not, go!
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the crisis arose, Ruizong mounted the Chengtian Tower. As ministers gradually gathered, the emperor waved and said, 'Those who help me stay; those who do not, go!

sentences.zh: 於是有投名自驗者。

translations.literal: Thereupon some cast their names in to prove themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon some cast their names in to prove themselves.

sentences.zh: 事平，玄宗得所投名，詔象先收按，象先悉焚之。

translations.literal: When the matter was settled Xuanzong obtained the cast names and ordered Xiangxian to investigate and punish; Xiangxian burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was settled Xuanzong obtained the cast names and ordered Xiangxian to investigate and punish. Xiangxian burned them all.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，欲並加罪，頓首謝曰：「赴君之難，忠也。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and wished to punish them all together; Xiangxian kowtowed and apologized: 'To go to the ruler's difficulty is loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angry and wished to punish them all together. Xiangxian kowtowed and apologized, 'To go to the ruler's difficulty is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 陛下方以德化天下，奈何殺行義之人？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now using virtue to transform the realm—how can you kill men who act righteously?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is just now using virtue to transform the realm—how can you kill men who act righteously?

sentences.zh: 故臣違命，安反側者，其敢逃死？」

translations.literal: Therefore your subject disobeyed the order to secure those who wavered—would they dare escape death?'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I disobeyed the order to secure those who wavered—would they dare escape death?'

sentences.zh: 帝寤，善之。

translations.literal: The emperor awoke to it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor awoke to it and approved.

sentences.zh: 時窮治忠、羲等黨與，象先密為申救，保全甚眾，當時無知者。

translations.literal: At the time the investigation of Zhizhong, Xi, and their factions was exhaustive; Xiangxian secretly pleaded for them and preserved very many, though at the time none knew.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the investigation of Zhizhong, Xi, and their factions was exhaustive. Xiangxian secretly pleaded for them and preserved very many, though at the time none knew.

sentences.zh: 罷為益州大都督府長史、劍南按察使，為政尚仁恕。

translations.literal: He was dismissed as chief administrator of the metropolitan prefecture of Yizhou and Jiannan inspection commissioner; his governance valued benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed as chief administrator of the metropolitan prefecture of Yizhou and Jiannan inspection commissioner. His governance valued benevolence and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 司馬韋抱真諫曰：「公當峻撲罰以示威，不然，民慢且無畏。」

translations.literal: The aide Wei Baozhen remonstrated: 'Your Lordship should use severe beating and punishment to show authority; otherwise the people will be lax and unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: The aide Wei Baozhen remonstrated, 'Your Lordship should use severe beating and punishment to show authority. Otherwise the people will be lax and unafraid.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「政在治之而已，必刑法以樹威乎？」

translations.literal: He replied: 'Government lies in governing—that is all. Must one use penal law to build authority?'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'Government lies in governing—that is all. Must one use penal law to build authority?'

sentences.zh: 卒不從，而蜀化。

translations.literal: He finally did not follow the advice, and Shu was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He finally did not follow the advice, and Shu was transformed.

sentences.zh: 累徙蒲州刺史，兼河東按察使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly moved to prefect of Pu and concurrently Hedong inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly moved to prefect of Pu and concurrently Hedong inspection commissioner.

sentences.zh: 小吏有罪，誡遣之，大吏白爭，以為可杖，象先曰：「人情大抵不相遠，謂彼不曉吾言邪？

translations.literal: A petty clerk had a crime and was admonished and sent away; a senior clerk reported in dispute that he could be beaten. Xiangxian said: 'Human feelings are mostly not far apart—do you think he does not understand my words?
translations.idiomatic: A petty clerk had a crime and was admonished and sent away. A senior clerk reported in dispute that he could be beaten. Xiangxian said, 'Human feelings are mostly not far apart—do you think he does not understand my words?

sentences.zh: 必責者，當以汝為始。」

translations.literal: If there must be punishment, I shall begin with you.
translations.idiomatic: If there must be punishment, I shall begin with you.

sentences.zh: 大吏慚而退。

translations.literal: The senior clerk withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The senior clerk withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「天下本無事，庸人擾之為煩耳。

translations.literal: He once said: 'Under Heaven there is originally no trouble—mediocre men stir it up into bother.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, 'Under Heaven there is originally no trouble—mediocre men stir it up into bother.

sentences.zh: 第澄其源，何憂不簡邪？」

translations.literal: Only clarify the source—why worry that things will not be simple?
translations.idiomatic: Only clarify the source—why worry that things will not be simple?

sentences.zh: 故所至民吏懷之。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever he went clerks and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore wherever he went clerks and people cherished him.

sentences.zh: 入為太子詹事，歷戶部尚書，知吏部選事，母喪免。

translations.literal: He entered court as guardian of the heir, served as minister of revenue, and held charge of Ministry of Personnel selections; he left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as guardian of the heir, served as minister of revenue, and held charge of Ministry of Personnel selections. He left office on his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 起為揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was recalled as chief administrator of the metropolitan prefecture of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as chief administrator of the metropolitan prefecture of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷太子少保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to junior guardian of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to junior guardian of the heir.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈尚書左丞相，謚曰文貞。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-two, was posthumously made left chief minister of the Secretariat, posthumous name Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two, was posthumously appointed left chief minister of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenzhen (Cultured and Upright).

sentences.zh: 始，象先名景初，睿宗曰：「子能紹先構，是謂象賢者。」

translations.literal: At first Xiangxian's name was Jingchu; Ruizong said: 'You can continue your forebears' structure—this is called emulating the worthy.'
translations.idiomatic: At first Xiangxian's name was Jingchu. Ruizong said, 'You can continue your forebears' structure—this is called emulating the worthy.'

sentences.zh: 乃賜名焉。

translations.literal: He was therefore granted the name.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore granted the name.

sentences.zh: 弟景倩為撫溝丞。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jingqian was magistrate of Fugou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jingqian was magistrate of Fugou.

sentences.zh: 河南按察使畢構覆州縣殿最，欲必得實。

translations.literal: The Henan inspection commissioner Bi Gou reviewed prefectures and counties for annual ratings and wished to obtain the facts with certainty.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan inspection commissioner Bi Gou reviewed prefectures and counties for annual ratings and wished to obtain the facts with certainty.

sentences.zh: 有吏言狀曰：「某強清，某詐清，惟景倩曰真清。」

translations.literal: A clerk reported: 'So-and-so forcibly pure, so-and-so falsely pure—only Jingqian is called truly pure.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk reported, 'So-and-so forcibly pure, so-and-so falsely pure—only Jingqian is called truly pure.

sentences.zh: 終監察御史。

translations.literal: He ended as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 景融長七尺，美姿質，寬中而厚外。

translations.literal: Jingrong was seven feet tall, handsome in bearing, broad within and generous without.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong was seven feet tall, handsome in bearing, broad within and generous without.

sentences.zh: 博學，工筆劄。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, skilled in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and skilled in letters.

sentences.zh: 以陰補千牛，轉新鄭令，政有風績，累遷工部尚書、東京留守。

translations.literal: He entered office by yin privilege as a thousand-bull guard, was transferred to magistrate of Xinzheng with marked governance, and was repeatedly promoted to minister of public works and eastern capital defender.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by yin privilege as a thousand-bull guard, was transferred to magistrate of Xinzheng with marked governance, and was repeatedly promoted to minister of public works and eastern capital defender.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈廣陵郡都督。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made military governor of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed military governor of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 景融於象先，後母弟也。

translations.literal: Jingrong to Xiangxian was a younger brother by the stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong to Xiangxian was a younger brother by the stepmother.

sentences.zh: 象先被笞，景融諫，不入，則自楚，母為損威，人多其友。

translations.literal: When Xiangxian was beaten Jingrong remonstrated; if not accepted he beat himself; the mother thereby lost authority; many praised their friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangxian was beaten Jingrong remonstrated. If not accepted he beat himself. The mother thereby lost authority, and many praised their friendship.

sentences.zh: 四世孫希聲。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation descendant Xisheng.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation descendant Lu Xisheng.

sentences.zh: 希聲博學善屬文，通《易》、《春秋》、《老子》，論著甚多。

translations.literal: Xisheng was broadly learned and skilled at literary composition, versed in the Changes, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Laozi, with many treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheng was broadly learned and skilled at literary composition, versed in the Changes, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Laozi, with many treatises.

sentences.zh: 商州刺史鄭愚表為屬。

translations.literal: The prefect of Shangzhou Zheng Yu memorialized him as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Shangzhou Zheng Yu memorialized him as a staff member.

sentences.zh: 後去，隱義興。

translations.literal: Later he left office and hid in Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left office and hid in Yixing.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為右拾遺。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned as right remonstrance officer.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was summoned as right remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 時憸腐秉權，歲數歉，梁、宋尤甚。

translations.literal: At the time the crafty and corrupt held power; harvests failed several years, and Liang and Song were especially hard hit.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the crafty and corrupt held power. Harvests failed several years, and Liang and Song were especially hard hit.

sentences.zh: 希聲見州縣刓敝，上言當謹視盜賊。

translations.literal: Xisheng saw prefectures and counties carved down and memorialized that thieves should be watched carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheng saw prefectures and counties carved down and memorialized that thieves should be watched carefully.

sentences.zh: 明年，王仙芝反，株蔓數十州，遂不制。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Xianzhi rebelled; the roots spread across dozens of prefectures and could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wang Xianzhi rebelled. The roots spread across dozens of prefectures and could not be controlled.

sentences.zh: 擢累歙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to prefect of She.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to prefect of She.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聞其名，召為給事中，拜戶部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong heard his name, summoned him as drafting officer, and appointed him vice minister of revenue and co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong heard his name, summoned him as drafting officer, and appointed him vice minister of revenue and co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 在位無所輕重，以太子少師罷。

translations.literal: In office he had no weight; he was dismissed as junior guardian of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In office he had no weight. He was dismissed as junior guardian of the heir.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞等兵犯京師，輿疾避難。

translations.literal: When Li Maozhen and others' troops violated the capital he took his illness and fled to escape danger.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Maozhen and others' troops violated the capital he took his illness and fled to escape danger.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made left vice director of the secretariat, posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed left vice director of the secretariat, with the posthumous name Wen (Cultured).

sentences.zh: 元方從父餘慶。

translations.literal: Yuanfang's cousin Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang's cousin Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 餘慶，陳右衛將軍珣孫，方雅有祖風。

translations.literal: Yuqing was grandson of Chen, right guard general Xun, refined and elegant with his grandfather's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing was grandson of the Chen right guard general Xun, refined and elegant with his grandfather's manner.

sentences.zh: 已冠，名未顯，兄玄表唶曰：「爾名宦不立，奈何？」

translations.literal: Already capped, his name was not yet known; his elder brother Xuanbiao clicked his tongue: 'Your name and office are not established—what is to be done?'
translations.idiomatic: Already capped, his name was not yet known. His elder brother Xuanbiao reproached him: 'Your name and office are not established—what is to be done?'

sentences.zh: 餘慶感激，閉戶誦書三年，以博學稱。

translations.literal: Stirred, Yuqing shut his door and recited books three years, and was known for broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred, Yuqing shut his door and studied for three years, and was known for broad learning.

sentences.zh: 舉制策甲科，補蕭尉。

translations.literal: He placed first in the policy examination and was appointed bailiff of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the policy examination and was appointed bailiff of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 累遷陽城尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to bailiff of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to bailiff of Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 武后封嵩山，以辦具勞，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu performed the feng on Mount Song, for his labor in preparations he was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu performed the feng on Mount Song, for his labor in preparations he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，靈、勝二州党項誘北胡寇邊，詔餘慶招慰，喻以恩信，蕃酋率眾內附。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenglì, the Tangut of Ling and Sheng prefectures induced northern barbarians to raid the border; an edict ordered Yuqing to summon and comfort them; he instructed them with grace and trust, and the tribal chiefs led their masses to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenglì era, the Tangut of Ling and Sheng prefectures induced northern barbarians to raid the border. An edict ordered Yuqing to summon and comfort them. He instructed them with grace and trust, and the tribal chiefs led their people to submit.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史、鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant censor and Phoenix Pavilion drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace attendant censor and Phoenix Pavilion drafter.

sentences.zh: 後嘗命草詔殿上，恐懼不能得一詞，降左司郎中。

translations.literal: The empress once ordered him to draft an edict in the hall; in fear he could not produce a single phrase and was demoted to left bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: The empress once ordered him to draft an edict in the hall. In fear he could not produce a single phrase and was demoted to left bureau director.

sentences.zh: 久之，封廣平郡公、太子右庶子。

translations.literal: After a long while he was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping and made right guardian of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping and made right guardian of the heir.

sentences.zh: 餘慶於寒品晚進，必悉力薦藉。

translations.literal: Yuqing toward men of cold rank and late advancement always exerted himself to recommend and support them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing toward men of humble rank and late advancement always exerted himself to recommend and support them.

sentences.zh: 人有過，輒面折，退無一言。

translations.literal: When people had faults he would rebuke them to their face; after retiring he said not a word.
translations.idiomatic: When people had faults he would rebuke them to their face. After retiring he said not a word.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為河南、河北宣撫使，薦富春孫逖、京兆韋述、吳興蔣冽、河南達奚珣，後皆為知名士。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan he was commissioner to pacify Henan and Hebei, recommending Fuchun's Sun Ti, Jingzhao's Wei Shu, Wuxing's Jiang Lie, and Henan's Daxi Xun—all later became renowned gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he was commissioner to pacify Henan and Hebei, recommending Sun Ti of Fuchun, Wei Shu of Jingzhao, Jiang Lie of Wuxing, and Daxi Xun of Henan—all later became renowned gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 遷大理卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief judge of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief judge of the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 終太子詹事，謚曰莊。

translations.literal: He ended as guardian of the heir, posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as guardian of the heir, with the posthumous name Zhuang (Solemn).

sentences.zh: 雅善趙貞固、盧藏用、陳子昂、杜審言、宋之問、畢構、郭襲微、司馬承禎、釋懷一，時號「方外十友」。

translations.literal: He was on excellent terms with Zhao Zhengu, Lu Zangyong, Chen Zi'ang, Du Shenyan, Song Zhiwen, Bi Gou, Guo Xiangwei, Sima Chengzhen, and the monk Huaiyi—at the time called the Ten Friends Beyond Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was on excellent terms with Zhao Zhengu, Lu Zangyong, Chen Zi'ang, Du Shenyan, Song Zhiwen, Bi Gou, Guo Xiangwei, Sima Chengzhen, and the monk Huaiyi—at the time called the Ten Friends Beyond Office.

sentences.zh: 餘慶才不逮子昂等，而風流敏辯過之。

translations.literal: Yuqing's talent did not reach Zi'ang and the others, but in grace and quick eloquence he surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's talent did not reach Zi'ang and the others, but in grace and quick eloquence he surpassed them.

sentences.zh: 初，武后時，酷吏用事，中宗朝，幸臣貴主斜封大行，啗利嗇禍之人，與相乾沒，雖亟貴驟用，而戮不反踵。

translations.literal: At first, under Empress Wu cruel law officers held power; in Zhongzong's court favored ministers and noble princesses practiced slanting seals broadly; men who devoured profit and hoarded disaster joined in mutual encroachment—though swiftly ennobled and suddenly used, execution followed without respite.
translations.idiomatic: At first, under Empress Wu cruel law officers held power. In Zhongzong's court favored ministers and noble princesses practiced slanting seals broadly. Men who devoured profit and hoarded disaster joined in mutual encroachment—though swiftly ennobled and suddenly used, execution followed without respite.

sentences.zh: 餘慶以道自將，雖仕不赫赫，訖無悔尤。

translations.literal: Yuqing conducted himself by the Way; though in office he was not illustrious, to the end he had no regrets.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing conducted himself by the Way. Though in office he was not illustrious, to the end he had no regrets.

sentences.zh: 子璪，字仲采。

translations.literal: His son Can, courtesy name Zhongcai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Can, styled Zhongcai.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，補長安尉，以清幹稱。

translations.literal: He passed the classics examination, was appointed bailiff of Chang'an, and was known for purity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the classics examination, was appointed bailiff of Chang'an, and was known for purity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 開元初，中朝臣子弟不任京畿，改新鄉令，人為立祠。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, sons of central court ministers could not serve the capital region; he was changed to magistrate of Xinxiang, and the people built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, sons of central court ministers could not serve the capital region. He was changed to magistrate of Xinxiang, and the people built a shrine for him.

sentences.zh: 用按察使宇文融薦，遷澠池令。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of inspection commissioner Yuwen Rong he was transferred to magistrate of Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of inspection commissioner Yuwen Rong he was transferred to magistrate of Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部郎中，柬躭騎使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the Bureau of War and made envoy bearing the golden pouch.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the Bureau of War and made envoy bearing the golden pouch.

sentences.zh: 還，除洛陽令，時車駕在洛，摧勒奸豪，人不敢犯，為中書令蕭嵩所器。

translations.literal: On his return he was made magistrate of Luoyang; at the time the imperial carriage was at Luo; he crushed and constrained powerful rascals so people did not dare offend; he was valued by chief minister Xiao Song.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made magistrate of Luoyang. At the time the imperial carriage was at Luoyang. He crushed powerful rascals so people did not dare offend. He was valued by chief minister Xiao Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩罷，佗宰相俾陰廉嵩短，璪曰：「與人交，過且不可言，況無有邪？」

translations.literal: When Song was dismissed, another chief minister had someone secretly investigate Song's faults. Can said: 'In dealing with people, faults should not be spoken of even if they exist—how much less when there are none?'
translations.idiomatic: When Song was dismissed, another chief minister had someone secretly investigate Song's faults. Can said, 'In dealing with people, faults should not be spoken of even if they exist—how much less when there are none?'

sentences.zh: 以是忤貴近，出為太原少尹。

translations.literal: For this he offended the powerful and was sent out as junior governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: For this he offended the powerful and was sent out as junior governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 累徙西河太守，封平恩縣男。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly moved to prefect of Xihe and enfeoffed as Baron of Ping'en.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly moved to prefect of Xihe and enfeoffed as Baron of Ping'en.

sentences.zh: 屬邑多虎，前守設檻阱，璪至，徹之，而虎不為暴。

translations.literal: His district had many tigers; previous prefects set cages and pits; when Can arrived he removed them, and the tigers did not run wild.
translations.idiomatic: His district had many tigers. Previous prefects set cages and pits. When Can arrived he removed them, and the tigers did not run wild.

sentences.zh: 王及善，洺州邯鄲人。

translations.literal: Wang Jishan was a native of Handan in Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jishan was a native of Handan in Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 父君愕，有沈謀。

translations.literal: His father Jun'e had deep stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun'e had deep stratagems.

sentences.zh: 隋亂，并州人王君廓掠邯鄲，君愕往說曰：「隋氏失禦，豪俊共救其亂，宜撫納遺氓而保全之，觀時變，待真主。

translations.literal: In the Sui turmoil, Wang Junkuo of Bingzhou plundered Handan; Jun'e went to persuade him: 'The Sui have lost control; heroes together rescue the disorder—you should soothe and gather the remnant people and preserve them, watch the times change, and await the true lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui turmoil, Wang Junkuo of Bingzhou plundered Handan. Jun'e went to persuade him, 'The Sui have lost control. Heroes together rescue the disorder. You should soothe and gather the remnant people and preserve them, watch the times change, and await the true lord.

sentences.zh: 足下無尺寸之地、兼旬之糧，劫眾而興，但恣殘剽，所過失望，竊為足下羞之。」

translations.literal: You have not a foot of territory or ten days' grain; you rise by robbing the masses and only indulge in cruel plunder—where you pass, hope is lost. I am secretly ashamed for you.'
translations.idiomatic: You have not a foot of territory or ten days' grain. You rise by robbing the masses and only indulge in cruel plunder—where you pass, hope is lost. I am secretly ashamed for you.'

sentences.zh: 君廓謝曰：「計安出？」

translations.literal: Junkuo apologized: 'Where does the plan come from?'
translations.idiomatic: Junkuo apologized, 'Where does the plan come from?'

sentences.zh: 答曰：「井陘之險可先取。」

translations.literal: He answered: 'The peril of Jingxing Pass can be taken first.'
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'The peril of Jingxing Pass can be taken first.'

sentences.zh: 君廓從其言，遂屯井陘山。

translations.literal: Junkuo followed his words and encamped on Mount Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Junkuo followed his words and encamped on Mount Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，與君廓偕來，拜君愕大將軍，封新興縣公，累遷左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the passes he came with Junkuo; Jun'e was appointed grand general, enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing, and repeatedly promoted to general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the passes he came with Junkuo. Jun'e was appointed grand general, enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing, and repeatedly promoted to general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 從太宗征遼，領左屯營兵，與高麗戰駐蹕山，死於陣，贈左衛大將軍、幽州都督、邢國公，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Following Taizong's campaign against Liaodong he led the Left Encampment troops; fighting Goguryeo at Mount Zhubi he died in battle and was posthumously made left guard grand general, military governor of Youzhou, Duke of Xing, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Following Taizong's campaign against Liaodong he led the Left Encampment troops. Fighting Goguryeo at Mount Zhubi he died in battle and was posthumously appointed left guard grand general, military governor of Youzhou, and Duke of Xing, with burial honors at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 及善以父死事，授朝散大夫，襲邢國公爵。

translations.literal: Jishan because his father died in service was granted Grand Master of Palace Attendance and inherited the dukedom of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Jishan because his father died in service was granted Grand Master of Palace Attendance and inherited the dukedom of Xing.

sentences.zh: 皇太子弘立，擢及善左奉裕率。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Hong was established, Jishan was promoted to left attendant of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Hong was established, Jishan was promoted to left attendant of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 太子宴於宮，命宮臣擲倒，及善辭曰：「殿下自有優人，臣茍奉令，非羽翼之美。」

translations.literal: At a palace banquet the crown prince ordered palace ministers to perform tumbling; Jishan declined: 'Your Highness has your own performers; your subject merely follows orders—not the beauty of wings.'
translations.idiomatic: At a palace banquet the crown prince ordered palace ministers to perform tumbling. Jishan declined, 'Your Highness has your own performers. I merely follow orders—not the beauty of wings.'

sentences.zh: 太子謝之。

translations.literal: The crown prince apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince apologized.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Gaozong heard of it and granted a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong heard of it and granted a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 除右千牛衛將軍，帝曰：「以爾忠謹，故擢三品要職。

translations.literal: He was made general of the Right Thousand-Bull Guard; the emperor said: 'Because you are loyal and careful, We therefore promote you to a third-rank key post.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the Right Thousand-Bull Guard. The emperor said, 'Because you are loyal and careful, I therefore promote you to a third-rank key post.

sentences.zh: 群臣非搜辟，不得至朕所。

translations.literal: Ministers, unless searched and summoned, may not reach Our person.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, unless searched and summoned, may not reach my person.

sentences.zh: 爾佩大橫刀在朕側，亦知此官貴乎？」

translations.literal: You wear the great horizontal blade at Our side—do you know how noble this office is?'
translations.idiomatic: You wear the great horizontal blade at my side—do you know how noble this office is?'

sentences.zh: 病免。

translations.literal: Illness led to dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led to dismissal.

sentences.zh: 召為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as minister of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of the guard.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，歷司屬卿。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era he served as director of the Bureau of Dependents.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuigong era he served as director of the Bureau of Dependents.

sentences.zh: 山東饑，詔為巡撫賑給使。

translations.literal: When Shandong suffered famine an edict made him commissioner to tour and relieve.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong suffered famine an edict made him commissioner to tour and relieve.

sentences.zh: 拜春官尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出為秦州都督、益州長史，加光祿大夫，以老病致仕。

translations.literal: He was sent out as military governor of Qin and chief administrator of Yi, added grand master of splendid virtue, and retired on old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military governor of Qin and chief administrator of Yi, added grand master of splendid virtue, and retired on old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 及善不甚文，而清正自將，臨事不可奪，有大臣節。

translations.literal: Jishan was not very literary, but pure and upright in self-conduct, unshakable in affairs, with a great minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Jishan was not very literary, but pure and upright in self-conduct, unshakable in affairs, with a great minister's integrity.

sentences.zh: 時二張怙寵，每侍宴，無人臣禮，及善數裁抑之，後不悅曰：「卿年高，不宜侍遊燕，但檢校閣中。」

translations.literal: At the time the two Zhangs relied on favor; whenever they attended banquets they showed no minister's ritual; Jishan repeatedly restrained them; the empress displeased said: 'You are old and should not attend pleasure excursions—only inspect the pavilion.'
translations.idiomatic: At the time the two Zhang brothers relied on favor. Whenever they attended banquets they showed no minister's ritual. Jishan repeatedly restrained them. The empress displeased said, 'You are old and should not attend pleasure excursions—only inspect the pavilion.'

sentences.zh: 及善即移病餘月，後不復問，嘆曰：「中書令可一日不見天子乎？」

translations.literal: Jishan immediately pleaded illness for more than a month; the empress no longer inquired; he sighed: 'Can a chief minister of the Secretariat go a day without seeing the Son of Heaven?'
translations.idiomatic: Jishan immediately pleaded illness for more than a month. The empress no longer inquired. He sighed, 'Can a chief minister of the Secretariat go a day without seeing the Son of Heaven?'

sentences.zh: 遂乞骸骨，猶不許，改文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: He then begged to retire; still not permitted; he was changed to left assistant director of the Secretariat and third rank with the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He then begged to retire but was still not permitted. He was changed to left assistant director of the Secretariat and third rank with the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十二，贈益州大都督，謚曰貞，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-two, was posthumously made metropolitan governor of Yi, posthumous name Zhen, and buried with honor at Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two, was posthumously appointed metropolitan governor of Yi, with the posthumous name Zhen (Upright), and buried with honor at Qianling.

sentences.zh: 李日知，鄭州滎陽人。

translations.literal: Li Rizhi was a native of Xingyang in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rizhi was a native of Xingyang in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 及進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 天授中，歷司刑丞。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era he served as aide in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou era he served as aide in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 時法令嚴，吏爭為酷，日知猶平寬無文致。

translations.literal: At the time laws were strict and clerks vied in cruelty; Rizhi remained even and lenient without literary prosecutions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time laws were strict and clerks vied in cruelty. Rizhi remained even and lenient without literary prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 嘗免一囚死，少卿胡元禮執不可，曰：「吾不去曹，囚無生理。」

translations.literal: He once spared a prisoner from death; vice director Hu Yuanli insisted it could not be done, saying: 'If I do not leave the office, the prisoner has no way to live.'
translations.idiomatic: He once spared a prisoner from death. Vice director Hu Yuanli insisted it could not be done, saying, 'If I do not leave the office, the prisoner has no way to live.'

sentences.zh: 日知曰：「仆不去曹，囚無死法。」

translations.literal: Rizhi said: 'If I do not leave the office, the prisoner has no way to die.'
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi said, 'If I do not leave the office, the prisoner has no way to die.'

sentences.zh: 皆以狀讞，而武后用日知議。

translations.literal: Both submitted their judgments, and Empress Wu used Rizhi's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Both submitted their judgments, and Empress Wu used Rizhi's opinion.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，為給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was made drafting officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was made drafting officer.

sentences.zh: 母老病，取急調侍，數日須發輒白。

translations.literal: His mother was old and ill; he took emergency leave to attend her; whenever he had to depart for several days he reported at once.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was old and ill. He took emergency leave to attend her. Whenever he had to depart for several days he reported at once.

sentences.zh: 母未及封而卒。

translations.literal: His mother died before the leave was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died before the leave was granted.

sentences.zh: 方葬，吏乃賫贈制，日知殞絕於道，左右為泣，莫能視。

translations.literal: Just as the burial was underway, clerks brought the grant edict; Rizhi collapsed on the road; those at his side wept and could not look.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the burial was underway, clerks brought the grant edict. Rizhi collapsed on the road. Those at his side wept and could not look.

sentences.zh: 巡察使路敬潛欲表其孝，使求狀，辭不報。

translations.literal: Inspection commissioner Lu Jingqian wished to memorialize his filial piety and sent someone to seek the documents; he declined and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection commissioner Lu Jingqian wished to memorialize his filial piety and sent someone to seek the documents. He declined and did not report.

sentences.zh: 服除，累遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: After mourning he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 日知貴，諸子方總角，皆通婚名族，時人譏之。

translations.literal: When Rizhi was noble his sons were still in their early years yet all married into famous clans; people of the time mocked this.
translations.idiomatic: When Rizhi was noble his sons were still in their early years yet all married into famous clans. People of the time mocked this.

sentences.zh: 後少子伊衡以妾為妻，鬻田宅，至兄弟訟鬩，家法遂替雲。

translations.literal: Later his youngest son Yiheng took a concubine as wife and sold fields and houses, until brothers sued one another in strife, and the family discipline was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Later his youngest son Yiheng took a concubine as wife and sold fields and houses until brothers sued one another in strife, and the family discipline was ruined.

sentences.zh: 杜景佺，冀州武邑人。

translations.literal: Du Jingqian was a native of Wuyi in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingqian was a native of Wuyi in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 性嚴正。

translations.literal: By nature stern and upright.
translations.idiomatic: By nature stern and upright.

sentences.zh: 舉明經中第。

translations.literal: He placed in the classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the classics examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 出為益州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was sent out as recorder of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as recorder of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 時隆州司馬房嗣業徙州司馬，詔未下，欲即視事，先笞責吏以示威。

translations.literal: At the time the Longzhou aide Fang Siye was transferred to prefectural aide; the edict had not yet been issued; he wished to assume duties at once and first beat and rebuked clerks to show authority.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Longzhou aide Fang Siye was transferred to prefectural aide. The edict had not yet been issued. He wished to assume duties at once and first beat and rebuked clerks to show authority.

sentences.zh: 景佺謂曰：「公雖受命為司馬，州未受命，何急數日祿邪？」

translations.literal: Jingqian told him: 'Though you have been ordered as aide, the prefecture has not yet received the order—why hurry for a few days' salary?'
translations.idiomatic: Jingqian told him, 'Though you have been ordered as aide, the prefecture has not yet received the order—why hurry for a few days' salary?'

sentences.zh: 嗣業怒，不聽。

translations.literal: Siye was angry and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Siye was angry and would not listen.

sentences.zh: 景佺曰：「公持咫尺制，真偽莫辨，即欲攪亂一府，敬業揚州之禍，非此類邪？」

translations.literal: Jingqian said: 'You hold a foot-long document whose authenticity cannot be distinguished and at once wish to stir up the whole prefecture—the disaster of Jingye at Yangzhou—is it not this kind?'
translations.idiomatic: Jingqian said, 'You hold a foot-long document whose authenticity cannot be distinguished and at once wish to stir up the whole prefecture—the disaster of Li Jingye at Yangzhou—is it not this kind?'

sentences.zh: 叱左右罷去，既乃除荊州司馬，吏歌之曰：「錄事意，與天通；

translations.literal: He shouted for attendants to remove him; in the end Siye was made aide of Jing; clerks sang: 'The recorder's intent reaches Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: He shouted for attendants to remove him. In the end Siye was made aide of Jing. Clerks sang, 'The recorder's intent reaches Heaven;

sentences.zh: 州司馬，折威風。」

translations.literal: the prefectural aide breaks imposing wind.'
translations.idiomatic: the prefectural aide breaks imposing wind.'

sentences.zh: 由是浸知名。

translations.literal: Thereby he gradually became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he gradually became renowned.

sentences.zh: 入為司刑丞，與徐有功、來俊臣、侯思止專治詔獄，時稱「遇除、杜者生，來、侯者死」。

translations.literal: He entered as aide in the Bureau of Punishments and with Xu Yougong, Lai Junchen, and Hou Sizhi specialized in edict prisons; at the time it was said: 'Meet Chu or Du and live; meet Lai or Hou and die.'
translations.idiomatic: He entered as aide in the Bureau of Punishments and with Xu Yougong, Lai Junchen, and Hou Sizhi specialized in edict prisons. At the time it was said, 'Meet Chu or Du and live; meet Lai or Hou and die.'

sentences.zh: 改秋官員外郎，與侍郎陸元方按員外郎侯味虛罪，已推，輒釋之。

translations.literal: He was changed to aide in the Bureau of Punishments; with vice minister Lu Yuanfang he investigated the crime of aide Hou Weiwei; already convicted, he then released him.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to aide in the Bureau of Punishments. With vice minister Lu Yuanfang he investigated the crime of aide Hou Weiwei. Already convicted, he then released him.

sentences.zh: 武后怒其不待報，元方大懼，景佺獨曰：「陛下明詔六品、七品官，文辨已定，待命於外，今雖欲罪臣，奈明詔何？」

translations.literal: The empress was angry that he did not await report; Yuanfang was greatly afraid; Jingqian alone said: 'Your Majesty's clear edict on sixth- and seventh-rank officials: once the documents are settled they await orders outside—now though you wish to punish your subject, what of the clear edict?'
translations.idiomatic: The empress was angry that he did not await report. Yuanfang was greatly afraid. Jingqian alone said, 'Your Majesty's clear edict on sixth- and seventh-rank officials: once the documents are settled they await orders outside. Now though you wish to punish me, what of the clear edict?'

sentences.zh: 宰相曰：「詔為司刑設，何預秋官邪？」

translations.literal: The chief minister said: 'The edict was set for the Bureau of Punishments—what has it to do with the Bureau of Punishments?'
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister said, 'The edict was set for the Bureau of Punishments—what has it to do with the Bureau of Punishments?'

sentences.zh: 景佺曰：「詔令一布，無臺、寺之異。」

translations.literal: Jingqian said: 'Once an edict is issued, there is no difference between terrace and ministry.'
translations.idiomatic: Jingqian said, 'Once an edict is issued, there is no difference between terrace and ministry.'

sentences.zh: 後以為守法，擢鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: The empress considered him law-abiding and promoted him to Phoenix Pavilion drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The empress considered him law-abiding and promoted him to Phoenix Pavilion drafter.

sentences.zh: 遷洛州司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to aide of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to aide of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 延載元年，檢校鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanzai he was acting vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanzai he was acting vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and co-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 後嘗季秋出梨華示宰相以為祥，眾賀曰：「陛下德被草木，故秋再華，周家仁及《行葦》之比。」

translations.literal: The empress once in late autumn produced pear blossoms and showed the chief ministers as auspicious; all congratulated: 'Your Majesty's virtue covers grass and trees, therefore autumn blooms twice—the Zhou family's benevolence reaching the Ode of Walking Rushes.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress once in late autumn produced pear blossoms and showed the chief ministers as auspicious. All congratulated, 'Your Majesty's virtue covers grass and trees, therefore autumn blooms twice—the Zhou family's benevolence reaching the Ode of Walking Rushes.'

sentences.zh: 景佺獨曰：「陰陽不相奪倫，瀆即為災。

translations.literal: Jingqian alone said: 'Yin and yang must not usurp each other's order; violation is disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqian alone said, 'Yin and yang must not usurp each other's order. Violation is disaster.

sentences.zh: 故曰：『冬無愆陽，夏無伏陰，春無淒風，秋無苦雨。』

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "In winter there is no excess yang; in summer no hidden yin; in spring no chill wind; in autumn no bitter rain."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said, 'In winter there is no excess yang; in summer no hidden yin; in spring no chill wind; in autumn no bitter rain.'

sentences.zh: 今草木黃落，而木復華，瀆陰陽也。

translations.literal: Now grass and trees yellow and fall, yet trees bloom again—this violates yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Now grass and trees yellow and fall, yet trees bloom again—this violates yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 竊恐陛下布德施令，有所虧紊。

translations.literal: I fear Your Majesty in spreading virtue and issuing orders has something awry.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Your Majesty in spreading virtue and issuing orders has something awry.

sentences.zh: 臣位宰相，助天治物，治而不和，臣之咎也。」
